5.2 The CGF Formalization
 The Context-Completion Governance Framework (CGF) gives the governance layer its
mathematical core [7]. the Orchestration Layer operates in a context-completion mode:
when the world presents incomplete context, the system must complete it under policy
while remaining answerable for the completion. The monograph models the resulting
governance posterior as a two-component mixture,
 ht = αt · π0 + (1 − αt) · π1,
 (6)
 where π0 is the verified-evidence component and π1 the unverified or adversarial
component, and αt ∈ [0, 1] is the weight the system currently places on verified evidence.
The dynamics of α are governed by a verification gain g — the rate at which incoming
evidence is verified — and a decay δ modeling the erosion of confidence in the absence of
fresh verification:
 E[αt+1] = αt + η g − δ αt,  so that  limt→∞ E[αt] = η g / δ.
 (7)
 The fixed point carries the governance lesson: sustained verification effort raises the
steady-state weight of verified evidence, but the equilibrium is proportional — let the
verification cadence lapse and the system slides toward its unverified component regardless
of its history. Three impossibility results delimit what any implementation can promise: (i)
incompleteness in the sense of Rice — no total, automatic decision procedure exists for
non-trivial semantic properties of the governed artifacts [12]; (ii) cryptographic
insufficiency — signatures and attestation prove origin and integrity, never semantic truth;
and (iii) a two-layer lower bound establishing that single-layer defenses cannot meet the
corpus's composited assurance target. These results are the formal reason the stack is
layered at all: boundaries between epistemics (VFG), execution (VTK), and governance
(the Orchestration Layer) are where the guarantees live.
5.3 The RLM Decision Rule and the Composited Bound
 At the enforcement layer, the RLM decision rule makes release/refusal decisions
conjunction-form — a release occurs only when the concrete risk residual is below


=== PAGINA 279 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 279
threshold, the actor's DID chain verifies, and the relevant ledger entries are complete:
 act ⟺ rconcrete ≥ τ  ∧  DID verified  ∧  ledger complete.
 (8)
 The composited assurance bound aggregates the layers' failure residuals into a single
statement the corpus reports as approximately 0.92:
 P(defense) ≥ 1 − εspec − εimpl ≈ 0.92,
 (9)
 where εspec and εimpl are the specification-level and implementation-level residuals
measured by the verification campaign of Section 5.4. The bound is deliberately modest: it
quantifies the gap the two-layer lower bound forces, and it is recomputed — not asserted —
whenever a component's residual changes, in keeping with the VFG rule that statuses are
data.
5.4 The VTK(N) Adversarial Evaluation
 the Orchestration Layer's assurance is empirical as well as formal. The VTK(N)
experiment runs a protocol with three phases — falsification attempts (F), provenance
verification (P), and hash-anchored response (H) — under three controls, with hypotheses
H1–H3 pre-registered before execution [7]. In the reported campaign, 1,000 synthetic
adversarial attacks were executed against the governance pipeline; the system defended
99.2% of them with a 4.2% false-positive rate at end-to-end latencies of 30–60 ms. The
formal verification campaign that accompanies the empirical one explored 10,243 states in
ProVerif for the protocol-level properties [27] and 87,421 states in TLA+ for the
system-level temporal properties [14], with higher-order properties discharged in Coq [28].
The implementation footprint — 28, 35, and 22 Rust crates across the three subsystems,
with 1,247 tests — and an external white-box audit engagement in the Cure53 class [29]
complete the assurance picture. The reader should note the epistemic posture these numbers
exhibit: the corpus reports its own defense rate as a measured value with a stated
false-positive cost, not as an absolute guarantee, consistent with the impossibility results
above.
5.5 ADR-018: External Verification of the Composition
 The second edition of the VTK–the Orchestration Layer documentation incorporates
the ADR-018 corpus — 3,527 lines recording the external verification of the architecture
against a threat model T1–T12 [8]. Nine components were verified by execution (not by
inspection), a schema v1.2 fixes the evidence record format, and a decision note records
what the exercise could and could not establish. ADR-018 matters to this monograph for a
methodological reason: it demonstrates the framework's central claim — that assertions
about the stack itself are subject to the same instrumentation as external claims — and it
supplies the invariant catalogue (I15–I420) whose entries carry falsifiers and statuses


=== PAGINA 280 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 280
exactly as Sections 3 and 7 prescribe. The catalogue's honest status distribution, including
entries that remain Unproven, is archived with the corpus [8].
6. Integration: One Verifiable Trust Stack
6.1 Composition Semantics
 The three layers integrate by division of epistemic labor. VFG defines what may be
claimed: the status semantics, the falsifier obligations, the evidence conditions. VTK
defines what may be executed: falsifiers, pipelines, ledger operations, and the kernel
guarantees underneath them. the Orchestration Layer defines who may act and what is
recorded: identity, provenance, gates, and deliberation. Figure 3 shows the resulting stack;
Table 3 makes the binding explicit. The composition is not a plumbing convenience — it is
required by the impossibility results of Section 5.2, since no single layer can
simultaneously decide semantic truth (bounded by Rice [12]), provide execution integrity
(bounded by specification residuals), and supply institutional legitimacy (a governance, not
a technical, property).

6.2 The Integrated Gate Flow
 Operationally, a claim traverses the stack as follows. A conjecture enters the ledger as
Unproven, registered with its falsifier, which is compiled into the VTK kernel and
exercised continuously by property-based testing and bounded model checking [18][16].
When evidence arrives, twin-instrument agreement (Eq. 4) or verified reduction (Eq. 3)
promotes the claim; every transition is signed and anchored through the Orchestration
Layer pipeline of Figure 2 and appended to the audit trail. Decision gates consult the ledger
at run time: an action whose precondition cites an Unproven claim is refused by
construction — the RLM rule of Eq. (8) makes refusal the default, not the exception.
Refutation events demote claims to Falsified, archive the counterexample as evidence, and
require successors to cite the refutation. The loop closes where it began: in documents,
whose every quantitative statement now carries a status, a number, and a falsifier identifier
— this monograph's own Table 5 and Table 6 being instances of the pattern.
6.3 Alignment with Governance Standards
 The stack was not designed against a regulatory checklist, but the mapping to the
dominant instruments is direct, and Table 4 summarizes it. For the NIST AI RMF's four
functions [19], VFG operationalizes Measure; the Orchestration Layer's gates
operationalize Manage; the ledger and deliberation surface (L5) give Govern its audit trail;
and the corpus registration discipline gives Map its inventory. For the EU AI Act's
high-risk obligations [20], the continuously maintained risk-management file maps to the
ledger's transition records (Article 9); logging to the Orchestration Layer audit trail (Article
12); human oversight to the L5 deliberation surface with refusal-by-default gates (Article
14); and accuracy/robustness to the measured-status regime with declared coverage (Article
15). For ISO/IEC 42001's management-system cycle [21], the ledger is the documented
information substrate and falsification events drive corrective action. The mapping's value
is reciprocal: the standards gain a machine-checkable substrate for their verbs, and the stack
gains a compliance vocabulary without changing its semantics.

7. Empirical Results Across Domains
 This section consolidates the empirical ledgers that the integrated stack has produced.
Three corpora are examined: the Space-Sector Falsification Program corpus of world
space-development conjectures [4], the Phantom Twist Program corpus for the Phantom
Twist low-visibility UAV research program [5][38], and the applied market-research
analytics corpus (the Tap ecosystem report) [39], with the ADR-018 external verification of
the Orchestration Layer composition providing a fourth, self-referential data point [8].
Where external anchors could be re-verified against primary sources during the preparation
of this monograph, they are cited; the re-verification itself surfaced one attribution error
(§7.1), which is reported and corrected here in the spirit of the discipline the stack
prescribes.
7.1 Case Study A: The Space-Sector Falsification Program
Ledger

milestones, international governance, orbital infrastructure, and national programs. Its final
status distribution is 6 Measured, 1 Reduced, 10 Unproven, and 2 Falsified — and the
distribution itself is the first finding: three quarters of public space-governance claims, at
the moment of registration, carry no admissible evidence beyond announcement, while
exactly two claims in the corpus were refuted by recorded events. Table 5 reproduces the
ledger in summary form.

 The two falsifications repay analysis. NTP-01 (DRACO): the joint NASA–DARPA
nuclear-thermal demonstration, registered as a flight conjecture, was refuted when NASA's
fiscal-year 2026 budget request zeroed the nuclear thermal and nuclear electric propulsion
lines and NASA described the decision as reflecting the partner's cancellation of the
mission [43]. The falsifier (falsify_ntp_01, Listing 1) fired on the cancellation event; the
ledger demoted the claim and archived the budget document as the refutation evidence.
MSR-01 (Mars Sample Return): the baseline architecture — sample return on the 2031
schedule — was refuted when Congress ended the existing program in January 2026 by
withholding funding, appropriating $110M for alternative architectures while leaving no
authorized lander, Mars ascent vehicle, or Earth-return spacecraft [44]. Both events are of


=== PAGINA 284 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 284
the kind that governance prose routinely absorbs without consequence ('the program is
being restructured'); the ledger absorbs them as refutations, which is the designed behavior.
 The re-verification pass also produced a correction. The corpus recorded the New
Glenn booster-reuse event (NG-01) as occurring on mission NG-2; contemporary reporting
establishes that the booster recovered after NG-2 was refurbished and reflown on NG-3, on
April 19, 2026 — the first New Glenn booster reuse — with the NG-3 upper stage
subsequently placing its payload in an incorrect orbit [41]. The date in the ledger is correct;
the mission attribution was not. Under the discipline's own rules, the corpus's claim
statement required a specification correction, which is now reflected in Table 5, and the
incident is logged in Section 8.3 among the framework's self-corrections. It is worth noting
that the upper-stage anomaly on the same flight strengthens, rather than weakens, the case
for per-claim instrumentation: 'launch vehicle reusable' and 'mission nominal' are different
claims with different falsifiers, and conflating them is exactly the assertion-inflation the
stack exists to prevent.
7.2 Case Study B: The Phantom Twist Ledger
 The Phantom Twist program — a single-propeller UAV whose airframe spins at
approximately 25 revolutions per second so that motion blur renders it nearly invisible to
cameras, published in the peer-reviewed Robotics: Science and Systems proceedings and
independently covered in the technical press [38][45] — exercises the stack inside a live
research project rather than over external programs. The dossier registers seven conjectures
PT-01 through PT-07, each with formulas (perceptual LPIPS thresholds [46], Kuramoto
synchronization dynamics [47], A-weighted acoustic envelopes [48]), Rust falsifiers, and
Kani harnesses; the final status distribution is 1 Measured, 2 Reduced, 3 Unproven, 1
Falsified [5]. Table 6 summarizes the ledger.

 Two features distinguish this ledger methodologically. First, PT-06 is documented as a
lifecycle: conjectured at a 0.5 W actuation-power formulation, held as Unproven, refuted by
empirical cross-validation (measured 0.086 W, outside the conjecture's admissible band),
and succeeded by PT-06′, which recalibrates the target to 0.1 W and enters the ledger as
Unproven — the state machine's no-silent-rehabilitation rule operating in practice. Second,
the corpus surfaces a measurement-theoretic trap worth generalizing: perceptual and
acoustic metrics are frequency-weighted, and at 50 Hz the IEC A-weighting curve
attenuates by approximately 30 dB, so a naive sound-pressure threshold would have
'confirmed' acoustic invisibility that the weighted threshold correctly withholds [48][5].
Instruments, in other words, are conjectures too, and the framework's instrument-inventory
discipline applies to its own meters.
7.3 Case Study C: Applied Analytics — The Tap Corpus
 The third corpus demonstrates transfer of the same discipline into commercial analytics
governance. The Tap ecosystem report audits 19 implementable improvements across three
products — Painel Tap, Análise TAP, and VisionCX — binding every quantitative claim to
an independently verified source (34 sources, tiered by credibility, with retrieval
timestamps) [39]. The verification surface is broad: market-research quality standards (ISO
20252:2019 [49]), Brazilian data-protection law's pseudonymization criteria via SHA-256
hashing (LGPD [50]), benchmark anchors for sentiment analytics (SemEval-2017 Task 4
[51]), and authorization frameworks (OAuth 2.0 [52]). Under the present integration, the
corpus's method is recognizable as VFG in enterprise dress: each improvement carries a
target number, a named instrument (benchmark, statute, or measurement protocol), and a
refutation condition — the falsifier written as an acceptance criterion in the delivery
pipeline rather than as Rust, which is the appropriate compilation target for that domain.

expectation, derived from the Goodhart taxonomy [22], that a measurable fraction of any
corpus's confident claims will not survive contact with instruments.

8. Counterarguments and Limitations
8.1 The Impossibility Backbone
 The most fundamental objection to a falsifier-first governance stack is that it cannot,
even in principle, verify everything — and the stack agrees. Rice's theorem guarantees that
no total automatic procedure decides non-trivial semantic properties of programs [12]; the
CGF's own results add cryptographic insufficiency and the two-layer lower bound (Section
5.2). The framework's response is to convert these limits into declared quantities —
coverage ρ(c) (Eq. 2), Kani unrolling bounds, information-gate margins — rather than to
minimize them rhetorically. The residual risk is real: a claim whose failure surface lies
largely outside a falsifier's declared domain enjoys only the protection of that domain, and
an auditor who does not read the declared coverage may over-trust. Declared coverage
makes the over-trust visible; it does not eliminate it.
8.2 Goodhart Vulnerability of the Falsifiers Themselves
 A second objection inverts the framework: if numbers become governance objects, the
numbers will be gamed. The taxonomy of Goodhart mechanisms [22] and the formalization
of reward hacking [23] both predict that optimization pressure on any proxy degrades it,
and falsifiers are proxies. The stack's mitigations are structural — falsifier inputs must be
instrument-derived rather than self-reported; twin-instrument agreement (Eq. 4) raises the


=== PAGINA 287 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 287
cost of gaming from one source to two; refutation events are immutable, so gaming leaves
forensic traces; and the Orchestration Layer identity layer binds numbers to accountable
actors [24][25]. None of this closes the loop completely: an adversary who controls the
instruments controls the ledger, which is why the design reserves external adversarial audit
(the Cure53-class engagement [29]) as a permanent, non-optional component rather than a
one-off milestone.
8.3 Corpus Limitations and the Self-Correction Record
 The empirical corpora have the limitations of their origin: a single research program, a
single principal author, and domain selection by opportunity rather than by sampling frame.
Inter-rater reliability for status assignment has not been measured, and the falsification rate
of Table 7 should be read as an existence demonstration, not an unbiased estimate.
Integration of the corpora surfaced and corrected five internal defects, which we report as
the framework's self-correction record: (i) the space corpus's headline count of 60 falsifiers
overstated the ledger, corrected to the 19 actually registered; (ii) its Reduced count of 3
reduced to 1 (DEB-01) under the strict definition of Eq. (3); (iii) the TOUR-01 conjecture
(commercial suborbital operations in Q4 2026) was downgraded from Measured to
Unproven, its prior status reflecting announcement rather than event; (iv) the ART-01
threshold had drifted between the corpus's prose and its table, unified here on the GAO
schedule assessment [40]; and (v) the NG-01 mission attribution (NG-2 → NG-3) corrected
during this monograph's re-verification [41]. The Phantom dossier reports analogous
double counts for its own ledger (initial 1M/2R/4U; final 1M/2R/3U/1F) [5]. That the
corrections exist is a limitation of the corpus; that they are enumerable, documented, and
propagated is the discipline working as specified.
8.4 External Validity, Verification Versus Validation, and
Source Decay
 Three further constraints bound the claims of this monograph. First, verification is not
validation: the stack can demonstrate that a claim's instruments agree and its falsifiers are
silent; it cannot demonstrate that the underlying requirement was the right one, which
remains a deliberative, political question that no architecture resolves. Second, external
validity is untested: whether the falsification-rate base rate transfers to corpora outside
space development, UAV research, and analytics governance is unknown. Third, the
web-mediated verification protocol inherits the biases and decay of its sources — anchors
are archived with retrieval timestamps precisely because URLs rot — and the assurance
campaign's headline numbers (99.2% defense; composited bound ≈ 0.92) are
corpus-measured values whose independent replication, though provided for by the
external-audit mechanism, has not yet been published. Finally, the standards mapping of
Table 4 is an analytic alignment, not a certification: conformance with the EU AI Act's


=== PAGINA 288 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 288
high-risk regime, for instance, requires the regulatory process itself [20], and no mapping in
this monograph should be read as substituting for it.
8.5 The Hallucination Vector in LLM-Assisted Pipelines
 A practical objection concerns the tooling era itself: much of the retrieval and drafting
around modern governance corpora is now language-model-assisted, and generative
models fabricate plausible citations and numbers [2]. The stack's position is that this vector
strengthens, rather than weakens, the case for the architecture: a pipeline in which every
numeric claim must arrive with an instrument and a falsifier identifier will reject a
hallucinated citation at registration time, because the ledger's schema has no slot for
unanchored numbers. The residual risk shifts to the human surface (prose summaries of the
ledger, such as this monograph), which is why the corpus documents maintain source-tier
labeling and access-date protocols [39], and why benchmarks themselves are treated as
falsifiable instruments rather than oracles [3].
9. Conclusion and Future Work
 This monograph set out to integrate three research artifacts — the VFG epistemic
discipline, the VTK formal kernel, and the Orchestration Layer governance layer — into a
single architecture for verifiable trust, and to consolidate the empirical evidence that the
integrated stack has produced. The integration is completed in the composition semantics
of Section 6: VFG defines what may be claimed, VTK what may be executed, the
Orchestration Layer who may act and what is recorded, and the boundaries between them
are the load-bearing walls that the CGF's impossibility results predict must exist. The
empirical consolidation of Section 7 shows the stack operating across three domains with a
consistent texture: roughly a quarter of registered conjectures reach Measured status, half
remain Unproven, and a ninth are refuted by recorded events — including two
program-level cancellations (DRACO, Mars Sample Return) and one research-target
recalibration (PT-06) that the framework detected, archived, and propagated without
editorial intervention.
 The broader lesson is epistemic before it is technical. Governance documents that
assert trust produce exactly the epistemic texture the space corpus measured — half
announcement, a quarter measurement, a ninth refutation — and the difference between
asserting and measuring is not attitude but infrastructure: statuses that are data, falsifiers
that are code, evidence that is content-addressed, and gates that refuse by default. The
discipline's slogan compresses the design into six words: the framework does not say yes or
no — it says show the number. The consolidated ledgers of this monograph are the number
that the discipline asks of itself.


=== PAGINA 289 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 289
 Future work proceeds on four fronts. First, multi-rater corpora: extending registration
to multiple independent raters with measured inter-rater reliability, converting the
falsification-rate statistic from an existence demonstration into an estimable base rate.
Second, falsifier synthesis: deriving falsifier skeletons mechanically from typed contracts
and specifications, so that the refutation path exists by construction at requirements time.
Third, gate policies in temporal logic: compiling the Orchestration Layer release rules into
TLA+ specifications with the same declared-bound discipline the kernel applies to code
[14]. Fourth, standardization: pursuing the certification path that ISO/IEC 42001 provides
[21] and contributing the ledger schema — statuses, coverage bounds, ΔH gates — as a
candidate substrate for the measurement provisions of the EU AI Act [20] and the NIST AI
RMF [19]. The open problems that matter most, however, are the ones this monograph can
only bound and declare: coverage that is always partial, instruments that are themselves
conjectures, and a world that will keep testing whether the stones hold.

PART XII — THE SPACE-SECTOR
FALSIFICATION PROGRAM
This part formalizes a portfolio of 19 conjectures about the 2026 global space sector, each
paired with a numerical threshold and an executable falsifier: a pure Rust function whose
output, evaluated over publicly verifiable events, decides whether the conjecture stands or
falls. The conjectures span launch systems and booster reuse, lunar and Mars exploration,
space-based solar power, orbital mining and manufacturing, commercial stations and
space tourism, debris removal, defense, and policy and national programs. Independent
documentary verification completed on September 19, 2026 maintained the dossier's
epistemic classes — 6 Measured / 1 Reduced / 10 Unproven / 2 Falsified — while issuing 8
metadata corrections to the source material, from the provenance of the GAO schedule
estimate to the signatory count of the Artemis Accords. The picture that emerges is a sector
whose dates and specifications are Measured while its frontier capabilities — orbital
refueling, sample return, solar power from orbit — remain Unproven or fall Falsified by
budgetary decision.
1. Introduction
 In September 2026, the global space sector presents an evaluative paradox that is rarely
named. On one side, the hardware and governance numbers are public and auditable: 72
countries have signed the Artemis Accords since September 14, with Türkiye as the 71st
[38][39]; a 172 mm liquid lens was fabricated aboard the International Space Station and
published in a peer-reviewed journal [36]; a New Glenn booster flew, landed, and flew
again [9][10]. On the other side, the operational capabilities that justify these investments
remain undemonstrated: there is still not a single propellant transfer between spacecraft in
orbit [5], two flagship programs — the nuclear thermal propulsion DRACO and Mars
sample return — have been formally cancelled [11][14], and the rejuvenated promise of
producing solar power in orbit awaits a washing-machine-sized satellite of 1 kW [18][19].
Dates and specifications are, in the vocabulary of this part, Measured; operational
capabilities remain Unproven — or transition to Falsified.
 This epistemic asymmetry has practical consequences. Investment committees, public
agencies, and policy makers treat announced schedules as if they were delivered
capabilities, and the sector has few standardized instruments for distinguishing the two
registers. The verification-first governance (VFG) framework — developed from
Popperian fallibilism [1] — proposes the opposite of promotional rhetoric: a claim has
empirical content only if it can be refuted by an objective test, and the test must be
executable by any third party. The Space-Sector Falsification Program materializes this


=== PAGINA 294 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 294
principle for space R&D: each conjecture (for example, “Artemis III occurs before 2027”)
receives an executable falsifier — a pure Rust function, with no dependencies, evaluated
over public events — and an epistemic state resulting from independent documentary
verification.
 This part makes three contributions. First, the formalization and classification of 19
concrete space conjectures, distributed across 15 domains (lunar and Mars exploration,
launchers and reuse, orbital energy and mining, stations and tourism, governance and
national programs) and across more than 20 countries and agencies, with the resolution of
each conjecture as of September 19, 2026. Second, the independent verification of the
program's source dossier, which corrected seven metadata items — dates, values, and
schedules — and demonstrates, within the research process itself, the refutation regime the
framework imposes (Section 5.3). Third, an explicit discussion of the limits of the method,
including the counting inconsistencies inherited from the dossier (15 domains and “60+
falsifiers” announced against the 19 formalized here) and the classificatory volatility
observed within the very month of September 2026.
 The thesis of this part is direct: space exploration is not a promise — it is a network of
verifiable dates, values, and specifications, each with an executable falsifier. When the
framework is applied with discipline, the global space portfolio of 2026 appears as it is: six
measured capabilities, one with partial evidence, ten still undemonstrated, and two falsified
by budgetary decision. The remainder of this part organizes that network: Section 2
presents the theoretical background, Section 3 the method, Section 4 the results conjecture
by conjecture, Section 5 the consolidated table and the verification adjustments, Section 6
the counterarguments, and Section 7 the conclusion.
2. Theoretical Background
2.1 Fallibilism and empirical content
 The philosophical foundation of VFG is Popper's fallibilism: an assertion has empirical
content only if it exposes itself to refutation by observation or test [1]. In the space context,
this requirement has a specific virtue: the sector produces discrete, dated, publicly
observable events — a launch, a landing, a booster recovery, a propellant transfer, a budget
law — that lend themselves naturally to the formalization of falsification conditions. Where
promotional discourse says “we are committed to orbital refueling”, the falsifier asks: how
many ship-to-ship demonstrations have been completed? The answer — zero as of August
2026 [5] — converts a narrative into a number, and the number into an epistemic state.
2.2 The VFG classes


=== PAGINA 295 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 295
 The framework operates with five operational epistemic states, defined by explicit
attribution rules (Section 3) and exemplified by this study's own portfolio. Table 1
summarizes the four classes applied to the conjectures analyzed; the fifth class, Proven, is
reserved for claims whose falsifier has been executed and published with independent
replication — the program's maturity target, not the current state of the conjectures
evaluated here.
Table 1 — VFG epistemic classes: operational definition and examples from the
portfolio

2.3 Relation to existing assessment practices
 The Space-Sector Falsification Program does not replace the existing instruments for
assessing space programs — it connects them to a common semantics. The Government
Accountability Office (GAO) reports on the Artemis programs already operate with
implicit falsifying logic: the estimate that, if HLS development took as many months as the
average of NASA's large projects, Artemis III would occur in early 2027 is, in practice, a
refutation condition on the official schedule [2]. Technology readiness levels (TRL), used
by agencies for decades, measure component maturity; VFG measures the epistemic
position of the system-level claim. Prediction markets, in turn, offer probabilistic
distributions for events that have not yet occurred [8] — a useful input, but no substitute for
the falsifier: probability is price, epistemic state is classification. The framework's
contribution is to unite these registers under a single rule: every relevant claim must be
rejectable by an objective, reproducible test.
2.4 Executable falsifiers
 The operational innovation of the Space-Sector Falsification Program is to treat the
falsifier not as a verbal criterion but as code: a pure Rust function, with explicit typing and
no external dependencies, whose signature exposes exactly the observable quantities that
decide the conjecture (launch year, number of demonstrations, returned mass, cancellation
boolean). Pure functions can be evaluated in any context and tested by property —


=== PAGINA 296 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 296
properties that, in future iterations of the program, can be verified by provers and model
checkers such as Kani over the classification code itself. The falsifier does not predict the
future: it records, at evaluation time, whether the required public event occurred. The
discipline lies in fixing, before the event, which event would count — and which would
count as failure.
3. Method
 The study followed a five-step protocol executed between August and September 19,
2026. Step 1 — inventory: extraction of the conjectures from the Space-Sector Falsification
Program dossier, each with a stable identifier (ART-01, REF-01, NG-01, NTP-01,
SBSP-01, AST-01, TOUR-01, STN-01, MSR-01, DEB-01, GD-01, MFG-01, GOV-01,
GOV-02, JP-01, RU-01, UAE-01, KR-01, BR-01). Step 2 — independent documentary
verification: for each conjecture, a search for a primary source (agency, company,
legislative body, or peer-reviewed periodical) and for at least one secondary source in the
specialized press, recording the access date (19/09/2026) and a clickable citation. Step 3 —
metadata correction: discrepancies between the dossier and the sources were recorded as
verification adjustments (Table 4, Section 5.3), never silenced. Step 4 — formalization of
the falsifier as a pure Rust function, preserving the signatures of the original dossier. Step 5
— final classification according to the rules of Table 1.
 The attribution rules deserve explicit statement, because it is in them that the discipline
of the method resides. A conjecture is Measured only with a completed event and a
primary source or dated public record — a plan does not count: Virgin Galactic is classified
Measured only for its verified commercial reopening (March–April 2026 [24][25]), not for
the resumption of flights, which is still a target and not an event (Section 4.4.2). It is
Reduced when dated instrumental evidence exists — a launch contract, completed
integration, a prior demonstration — without the target event. It is Unproven when the
conjecture stands without a validating event as of the cutoff date. It is Falsified when
cancellation or budgetary unfeasibility is formal and documented — the mechanism that
determined this study's two falsifications.
 Three delimitations complete the method. First, the result is a momentary statistical
snapshot, dated September 19, 2026; class transitions are expected and desirable, and the
volatility observed within the very month — the Artemis Accords moved from 71 to 72
signatories on September 14 [38] — is a property of the object, not a defect of the method.
Second, verification privileged English- and Portuguese-language sources; primary sources
in Russian, Arabic, and Korean were accessed via the specialized press and translated
institutional pages, which may introduce detail lag. Third, the falsifiers formalize the
minimal failure condition of each conjecture as stated in the source dossier; specification


=== PAGINA 297 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 297
refinements (for example, defining refueling “demonstration” by minimum mass
transferred) are recorded as future work, not as silent decisions.
4. Results
 The results are presented conjecture by conjecture, grouped into five thematic domains.
Each subsection records the formal conjecture (stable identifier), the epistemic resolution
as of September 19, 2026, the verified data with the corresponding sources, and the
executable falsifier. The corrections introduced by independent verification appear inline
and are consolidated in Table 4 (Section 5.3).
4.1 Lunar and Mars exploration
4.1.1 ART-01 — Crewed lunar return (Artemis III)
 Conjecture: Artemis III occurs before 2027. Resolution: Unproven — falsified for
2026, standing for 2027. Three records compose the resolution. First, the GAO estimate
that, if HLS development took as many months as the average of NASA's large projects,
Artemis III would occur in early 2027 — technical note: this estimate comes from the
GAO-24-107249 report of November 2023 [2], not from a March 2026 report as the dossier
dated it; the content of the citation is preserved, the provenance was corrected. Second, on
February 27, 2026, NASA announced the reconfiguration of the flight sequence: Artemis
III was redesignated as a crewed demonstration mission in low Earth orbit — including
docking with the lunar lander — and the first crewed lunar landing now falls to Artemis IV,
with a declared target of 2028 [3][4]. Third, the launch of the mission itself remains
formally scheduled for mid-2027.
 The ART-01 falsifier encodes the original conjecture: it returns false (conjecture not
falsified) as long as the launch year does not exceed 2027. Verification shows that the
conjecture survived the 2026 cutoff by the narrowest possible margin — and that its
survival has already entailed a redefinition of what “Artemis III” means.
Listing 1 — falsify_art_01: executable falsifier for conjecture ART-01
/// ART-01: Artemis III occurs before 2027.
pub fn falsify_art_01(launch_year: u32) -> bool {
launch_year > 2027
}
// Result: launch_year = 2027 -> NOT falsified (limit)
// But if it is 2028 -> FALSIFIED
4.1.2 REF-01 — Orbital refueling (Starship)
 Conjecture: Starship performs ship-to-ship propellant transfer in orbit before 2027.
Resolution: Unproven. SpaceX demonstrated intra-vehicle transfer of roughly 10 tonnes of


=== PAGINA 298 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 298
LOX on previous flights, but the ship-to-ship demonstration remains future: the corporate
update of August 2026 still describes transfer between ships as a 2026 test-flight target tied
to HLS, without an exact date [5]. The scale estimates converge: executing the Artemis
mission with Starship HLS requires on the order of 15 refueling launches [6], with public
estimates ranging from 4 to 19 per lunar landing [7]. Dedicated prediction markets quoted,
in mid-September 2026, the ship-to-ship demonstration in 2026 as an uncertain event, on
the order of 50% [8].
Listing 2 — falsify_ref_01: executable falsifier for conjecture REF-01
/// REF-01: Starship performs propellant transfer in orbit.
pub fn falsify_ref_01(demos_completed: u64) -> bool {
demos_completed == 0
}
// Result: demos_completed = 0 (through July 2026)
// -> REF-01 is UNPROVEN
4.1.3 NTP-01 — Nuclear thermal propulsion (DRACO)
 Conjecture: DRACO demonstrates nuclear thermal propulsion (NTP) in orbit by 2027.
Resolution: Falsified. The DRACO program — a DARPA–NASA partnership that planned
to launch an NTP demonstrator in 2027 — was cancelled: NASA's budget proposal for
fiscal year 2026 zeroed out funding for nuclear thermal and nuclear electric propulsion
[12], NASA described the decision as reflecting the “partner's decision to cancel” the
mission [13], and the cancellation was reported in June 2025 [11]. This is the cleanest
falsification in the portfolio: the conjecture did not fail technically — it was removed from
the budget before any flight, illustrating that in government programs the appropriator of
resources is the final arbiter of the conjecture.

4.2 Launch vehicles and reuse
4.2.1 NG-01 — New Glenn booster reuse
 Conjecture: New Glenn reuses a booster successfully. Resolution: Measured. On April
19, 2026, on the vehicle's third flight, Blue Origin reused the “Never Tell Me the Odds”
booster — launched and recovered on the NG-2 mission in November 2025 — with
mission success and confirmed recovery [9][10]. Reuse was the vehicle's central economic
premise; the company told the specialized press that, to sustain the 2026 cadence, it expects
to reuse the booster every 30 days [9]. The event converts the conjecture into a dated record
observable by third parties — the exact pattern of a Measured claim.

4.2.2 JP-01 — The Japanese H3 launcher
 Conjecture: the H3 performs a successful launch. Resolution: Measured. The
JAXA/Mitsubishi Electric H3 consolidated its recovery from a turbulent development in
2026: Flight 6, on June 11–12, placed six small satellites in orbit and marked the return to
flight after the December 2025 failure [43][44]; Flight 9, on August 11, inserted the
Michibiki-7 navigation satellite into its target orbit 29 minutes after launch [45]. The
dossier's conjecture mentioned the “sixth flight” as the milestone; verification confirms the
event and adds the ninth flight as a second Measured datapoint in the same semester —
evidence of cadence, not chance.

4.3 Energy, mining, and manufacturing in orbit
4.3.1 SBSP-01 — Space-based solar power (OHISAMA)
 Conjecture: Japan demonstrates power transmission from orbit to Earth in 2026.
Resolution: Unproven. The OHISAMA demonstrator — a ~180 kg satellite the size of a
washing machine, planned for a 400 km orbit — has launch planned for 2026 and aims to
demonstrate the conversion and transmission of ~1 kW of space solar power, with
reception by 13 antenna stations in Suwa [18][19]. As of the cutoff date there is no public
record of launch or successful transmission: the expected event did not occur, and the
conjecture stands — with the caveat that the 1 kW demonstration is, by design, a proof of
concept, not a grid capability.

Unproven, and the 2026 mission is the next decisive event.

4.3.3 MFG-01 — In-orbit optical manufacturing (Fluidic Shaping)
 Conjecture: Fluidic Shaping produces a 172 mm lens. Resolution: Measured. Two
experiments performed aboard the ISS during the Ax-1 mission (April 2022) demonstrated
the Fluidic Shaping technique — which exploits surface tension in microgravity to shape
optical components — including a water lens of 172 mm diameter [37]. The results were
published in the peer-reviewed journal npj Microgravity of the Nature group [36];
verification note: the publication is from 2025, not from 2026 as the dossier dated it. It is
the only item in the portfolio whose evidence has academic form — a dated physical event,
a dimensional measurement, and a peer-reviewed publication — and it therefore serves as
the gold standard of what this framework considers Measured.

formulated with a floor of 61 — is not merely true but comfortably so: the floor falsifier

4.5.2 GOV-02 — The COPUOS LTS guidelines

design to disposal [41]; Guideline A.1 calls for limiting debris generation [41]. The
disposal regime evolves: the guidelines recommend disposal within 25 years after mission
end for LEO, and the U.S. FCC tightened the rule to 5 years for U.S.-licensed satellites

with no schedule to slip.

5.2 Epistemic asymmetry and falsification mechanisms
 Reading of the portfolio confirms the asymmetry that motivated the study, now with
measurable contours. All six Measured conjectures are observed hardware or normative
governance — booster reuse, flights of a consolidated launcher, lens fabrication, signatory
counts, adoption of guidelines, commercial reopening. No frontier operational capability —
orbital refueling, space-based solar power, asteroid mining, orbital interception,
commercial station — is Measured. The pattern suggests that the industry's bottleneck is
not building hardware that flies but closing the operational cycle that generates value: the
same vehicle that reuses boosters successfully has not yet transferred propellant between
ships [5][9].
 The second finding is the dominant falsification mechanism. The two Falsified
conjectures in the portfolio — DRACO and Mars Sample Return — were not refuted
technically: they were cancelled by budgetary decision [11][14]. In government programs,
therefore, the appropriator of resources functions as the court of last resort for conjectures,
and any verification framework must include legislative and budgetary events as first-class
falsifying events — exactly what the NTP-01 and MSR-01 falsifiers do by receiving a
cancellation boolean.

6. Counterarguments and Limitations
6.1 Minimalist falsifiers
 The most direct technical objection is that few-line boolean functions formalize the
conjecture at its coarsest level: falsify_ref_01 asks “zero or non-zero?”, whereas refueling
engineering would distinguish complete from partial transfer, by mass, duration, and
cryogenic purity. The objection is valid — and the trade-off is conscious. Minimalist
falsifiers are auditable by any reader, evaluable over public event feeds, and stable over
time; rich specifications require proprietary telemetry and third-party arbitration. The
program's evolution agenda is to marry the two registers: parameterized versions of the
falsifiers (minimum mass transferred, capture duration, target orbit) with formal
verification of the properties of the classification code itself — the same Kani/proptest
pattern applied in the rest of the VFG ecosystem. Until then, minimalism is a declared
limitation, not a hidden virtue.
6.2 Counting inconsistencies in the dossier


=== PAGINA 309 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 309
 Applying the framework's discipline to the source material itself, three counting
inconsistencies were identified and remain declared, not reconciled. First: the dossier
announces 15 domains but formalizes 19 conjectures — in practice each conjecture
occupies a domain of its own, and two Reduced domains (IRIS² and Gaganyaan) receive no
dedicated conjecture (Section 4.5.6). Second: the program announces “60+ executable
falsifiers”, but this part exhibits 19; the others are roadmap, not evidence — which is why
Table 3 classifies the 60+ as Unproven. Third: the dossier's summary table lists 3 Reduced
domains (including IRIS² and Gaganyaan), whereas the formalized portfolio contains 1
Reduced conjecture. The recommended resolution is the publication of a
version-by-version index of the falsifiers, with traceability from conjecture → domain →
source → status.
6.3 Snapshot and volatility
 The result is a dated snapshot, and the very month of September 2026 demonstrates the
volatility: the Artemis Accords moved from 71 to 72 signatories between the drafting of the
dossier and the completion of this part [38], and Virgin Galactic's target for resuming
flights slipped from Q4 2026 to February 2027 [26]. Epistemic classes are transient
attributions by design: Unproven can become Measured within a week. The falsifier freezes
the decision condition — not the world. The operational recommendation is quarterly
re-evaluation of the portfolio with automated evaluation of the falsifiers over public launch
and budget event feeds, making the framework continuous rather than punctual.
6.4 Sources and latency
 Verification combined primary sources (agencies, companies, legislative bodies,
peer-reviewed journals) with the specialized press, and the primary source was not always
accessible in public text: acts of the Russian, Arabic-speaking, and Korean governments
were accessed via specialized coverage and translated institutional pages, which introduces
latency and detail risk — the corrections in Table 4 illustrate the cost of that path.
Additionally, prediction markets offer useful probabilistic aggregation [8], but they reflect
attention prices, not evidence: no market number was used as the basis of any class in this
part.
6.5 Selection bias and Goodhart risk
 The portfolio was selected for narrative relevance and falsifier availability — not by
statistical sampling — so aggregate inferences beyond the snapshot (for example,
proportions of Measured “in the sector”) would be unwarranted. There is also an inverted
Goodhart risk: if the program's success metric becomes “proportion of falsifiers in OK”,
there will be an incentive to select conjectures easy to satisfy. The recommended mitigation
is preregistration of the complete portfolio (the 60 announced conjectures) before the next
evaluation round, with public admission criteria.


=== PAGINA 310 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 310
6.6 Probability and classification are distinct registers
 An elegant counterargument holds that prediction markets solve the problem without
falsifiers: if the market quoted ~50% for the 2026 refueling demonstration [8], the
uncertainty is already priced in. The argument conflates two registers. Probability is the
aggregated quotation of an uncertainty; epistemic class is the position of a claim before a
refutation condition. An event with 99% market probability remains Unproven until it
occurs — and an event with 1% that occurs is Measured. The framework does not dispense
with probability; it prevents probability from disguising the absence of evidence.
7. Conclusion and Implications
 This part formalized the Space-Sector Falsification Program and applied it to the global
space sector with a cutoff of September 19, 2026. The result is a network of conjectures
with explicit decisions: 6 Measured, 1 Reduced, 10 Unproven, 2 Falsified. The numbers
that remain, once rhetorical noise is removed, are these: 72 signatories of the Artemis
Accords; 172 mm of lens fabricated in orbit and published in a peer-reviewed journal; 1
New Glenn booster reused; 0 demonstrations of orbital ship-to-ship refueling; 2 flagship
programs cancelled by budgetary decision. Space exploration is not a promise — it is a
network of verifiable dates, values, and specifications, each with an executable falsifier.
 The implications are three. For investors, the difference between Measured and
Unproven is, literally, the sector's risk premium: the same ecosystem that reuses boosters
has not demonstrated the capability that underpins its most ambitious business cases, and
the portfolio formalized here provides the ruler for pricing that gap. For agencies and
policy makers, the falsifiers function as a transparency contract: a conjecture whose failure
condition is public and executable imposes a reputational cost on late retraction — the
DRACO and MSR falsifications show that the cost of early honesty is smaller than that of
indefinitely extended expectation. For the VFG program itself, the verification adjustments
of Table 4 set the agenda of the next iteration: publish the 60 announced falsifiers,
automate evaluation over public event feeds, and submit the classification code itself to
formal property verification.
 VFG discipline is not saying “yes” or “no” — it is saying “show the number”. Applied
to space, it transforms promotional discourse into a table with 19 rows, five columns, and
no opinions: conjecture, class, falsifier, status, source. What is real and what is aspiration
cease to be a matter of narrative and become a matter of record.

PART XIII — APPLIED GOVERNANCE IN
THE MARKET-RESEARCH ECOSYSTEM:
THE TAP CASE
This part applies the verification-first governance (VFG) methodology to a market-research
platform ecosystem, the Tap case: a respondent panel, an analytics platform and a
customer-experience platform. It specifies nineteen implementable improvements across
trust and compliance, data and measurement, and platform and AI, each with a concrete
implementation, an estimated cost, and a falsifier — an objective failure criterion that
publicly invalidates the claimed gain if it fails. Every proposal is grounded in verified
external sources (ISO 20252, ESOMAR, LGPD, the NPS architecture, BI connectors, public
machine-learning benchmarks), and domain-transfer limitations are declared where
external evidence does not fully support a claim. A prioritization matrix, a three-phase
18-month roadmap with falsifier-based exit gates and six global success metrics organize
execution. The part preserves the source report's budget reconciliation note, keeping both
the declared and the recalculated number sequences fully auditable.
Executive Summary
 This report presents nineteen implementable improvements for the ecosystem
composed of the Tap Panel, Tap Analysis and VisionCX, organized in four layers (product,
analysis, customer experience and cross-cutting integration). The starting point is the
preceding verification-first governance (VFG) analysis, which classified the main claims of
the three products into epistemic statuses — Measured, Reduced, Unproven and Proven —
and concluded that the ecosystem's competitiveness depends less on adding features and
more on converting unverifiable promises into public evidence. The VFG discipline does
not say “yes” or “no”: it says “show the number”. Each improvement proposed here
therefore follows a three-part structure: it solves an identified problem, has a concrete
implementation, and carries a falsifier — an objective criterion that, if it fails, publicly
invalidates the claimed gain.
 To ensure that the proposals are not mere statements of intent, all improvements were
grounded in verifiable external sources, researched in September 2026: international
research-quality standards (ISO 20252:2019), the ESOMAR due-diligence questionnaire
for online samples, the Brazilian General Data Protection Law (Law No. 13,709/2018) and
the Receita Federal's open-data catalogs, public machine-learning benchmarks
(SemEval-2017 Task 4, OpenML and RCAEval), peer-reviewed literature on respondent
quality, explainability and active learning, and official platform documentation
(Meta/WhatsApp, LinkedIn, Tableau, Looker and Power BI). Where the external evidence


=== PAGINA 315 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 315
does not fully support a claim — for example, in transferring the RCAEval benchmark,
designed for microservices, to root-cause analysis in surveys — the limitation is stated
explicitly.
 The total estimated investment is on the order of R$ 3.5 million distributed across three
phases over 18 months. Phase 1 (foundation, months 0–3) concentrates six low-cost
improvements — approximately R$ 260 thousand to R$ 340 thousand, according to the
reconciliation note in Section 8 — that turn credibility into competitive advantage: the
VFG transparency program, the published time baseline, public AI benchmarks, the public
panel audit, the Closed Loop with SLA, and export to R/Python/Stata. Phase 2
(differentiation, months 3–9) builds defensible advantages — respondent quality score, AI
explainability, root cause with human feedback, unified SSO, Meta-approved templates,
CRM API and analyst certification. Phase 3 (scale, months 9–18) serves enterprise clients
with predictive churn, a unified data pipeline, a template marketplace, BI export and
external data.
 The 12-month global goal is to raise the proportion of falsifiers in OK status from 8/19
(42%) to 17/19 (89%), with client retention ≥ 85%, mean time to first insight ≤ 5 minutes
and a Closed Loop resolution rate ≥ 80%. The immediate recommendation is to approve
and start the six P0 improvements within the current quarter: without them, the ecosystem
remains a bundle of unverifiable promises — the exact opposite of the VFG discipline it
claims to practice.
Keywords: VFG; panel quality; AI benchmarks; Closed Loop; LGPD; falsifiers; product prioritization.
1. Context and Purpose
 The Tap ecosystem operates three complementary products along the
market-intelligence chain. The Tap Panel is the digital respondent panel with a claimed 19
million members in Brazil, responsible for recruitment, incentives and response collection
for quantitative and qualitative research. Tap Analysis is the analytics platform that turns
raw responses into insights, with capabilities such as Smart Discovery, sentiment analysis,
root-cause analysis and the commercial claim of “70% more agility” relative to manual
workflows. VisionCX is the customer-experience platform, which operationalizes metrics
such as NPS and CSAT, deploys surveys through channels such as WhatsApp, and
conducts loop closure with detractor, passive and promoter clients.
 The VFG analysis mapped the public claims of the three products and assigned an
epistemic status to each. Measured claims have internal measurement but may lack external
audit — the case of the 19 million respondents. Reduced claims express direction and order
of magnitude without a published baseline — the case of the low friction rate and the 70%


=== PAGINA 316 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 316
agility gain. Unproven claims have no public evidence at all yet — the case of the AI
capabilities (Smart Discovery, sentiment and root cause) and of the integration between the
products. Table 1 summarizes the starting point and links each weakness to the
improvements that address it.
