5.1 Neuroscience: plasticity, reward, memory, and
autonomy
 Four principles with a direct counterpart in agent governance are inherited from
neuroscience. First, plasticity — the capacity to learn, formalized since Hebb (1949) — is
necessary for adaptation and dangerous without containment; invariant INV-NEURO-01
establishes that every update of weights, capabilities, or policies must preserve the
constitutional invariants, with a clear falsifier: any update that alters an invariant without
quorum. This formulation connects to a lineage of AI safety work that subordinates
self-modification to explicit constitutions, from Anthropic's Constitutional AI (2022) to


=== PAGINA 412 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 412
contemporary proposals for formally constrained self-modification envelopes cited in the
project documentation (Oliveira, 2026c). Second, the reward signal that guides
reinforcement learning (Sutton and Barto, 2018) is, in the trading context, a governance
signal: INV-NEURO-02 requires that every reward signal used to update policies be logged
and verifiable, avoiding reward hacking. Recent research corroborates the need: the
Alignment Auditor framework reframes reward inference from an estimation task into a
comprehensive verification process, structuring the audit in Bayesian stages (Bou et al.,
2025). Third, persistent memory must be versioned and verifiable (INV-NEURO-03) — a
requirement the WormGraph meets through chained record hashes, in the lineage of
Hopfield's (1982) associative systems and of the recurrent long-term memories of
Hochreiter and Schmidhuber (1997). Fourth, autonomy must be limited by fail-closed
containment (INV-NEURO-04): like the neuronal firing threshold formalized by
McCulloch and Pitts (1943), the agent executes only what its declared capabilities and
resource limits authorize; absence of authorization is denial, never grant.
 Two neural concepts complete the vocabulary. Predictive coding — the hypothesis that
the brain minimizes prediction error across hierarchies (Rao and Ballard, 1999; Friston,
2010), a formalization to which variational inference gives a probabilistic basis (Kingma
and Welling, 2013) — grounds the VTK's operational principle of verifying execution, not
reasoning: the system predicts the outcome of a verification, compares it with the actual
execution, and treats surprise as an investigation signal, not as noise. And stigmergy —
coordination through modification of the environment, demonstrated in recent simulations
in which societies of LLM agents build persistent technological portfolios through physical
marks in the world, more resilient than isolated search (Pal, 2026) — inspires reading the
WormGraph as a stigmergic environment: each recorded event is a mark that informs
future agents without direct communication, and the removal of agents does not destroy the
coordination infrastructure they left recorded (Oliveira, 2026c).
5.2 Nanonetworks: detection under noise and channel
memory
 Molecular communication in nanonetworks offers the grounding's most rigorous
formalism. Pierobon and Akyildiz (2011) characterized the noise sources of
diffusion-based communication — particle sampling noise, counting noise, and
ligand-receptor kinetics — showing that reliable detection requires a detector matched to
the channel's specific modulation. The transposition to the VTK is direct (Oliveira, 2026d):
sampling noise corresponds to network and IPC noise between components; counting
noise, to the variance in the count of witnesses of a quorum; ligand-receptor noise, to the
mismatch between trust key and signature scheme. Three invariants derive from this
correspondence: INV-NANO-01 (every recognizer must reject evidence that does not


=== PAGINA 413 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 413
reduce error — acceptance based on a non-discriminant signal is a failure); INV-NANO-03
(a detector matched to the signature scheme is mandatory — generic verifiers that accept
any scheme are channels without a detector); and INV-NANO-02 (route failure must be
reported as a missing leaf, not as silent corruption — distinguishing absence from
tampering is a condition for honest diagnostics). The same authors' 2012 extension
expresses the capacity of a channel with memory and molecular noise, showing that
channel memory limits what can be transmitted (Pierobon and Akyildiz, 2012); the
systemic analogue is the WormGraph's state memory, whose persistence creates
interference between events — and whose honest modeling requires acknowledging that
interference, not ignoring it. The closing invariant, INV-NANO-04, establishes that
detection, authentication, and destination binding must fail together: an artifact accepted
with two of the three properties is a system failure, in the same domain-separation logic
that RFC 6962 applies to leaves and inner nodes of the Merkle tree (Laurie, Langley, and
Kasper, 2013; Merkle, 1979). Regulatory networks complete the nano-digital mapping:
methods for inferring transcription factor activity in single cells, such as Epiregulon,
estimate interaction weights — activation or repression — whose small variation alters the
regulatory fate of the system (Włodarczyk et al., 2025); transposed to governance, the
analogy requires that every invariant have a falsifier sensitive to small changes
(INV-TRANS-01) and that every regulatory interaction be explicitly classified
(INV-TRANS-02) (Oliveira, 2026d).
5.3 Redox: honest status as a controlled ratio
 The third pillar is redox biology. Sies (2021) systematizes the concept of oxidative
eustress: healthy homeostasis is not the absence of oxidants but the maintenance of
controlled ratios — such as the NADPH/NADP+ ratio, which under physiological
conditions stays above ten to one and collapses under stress — within a dynamically
monitored window. The methodological transposition yields invariant INV-REDOX-01:
the verification status of a system is a controlled ratio, not a binary. Declarations of the
“everything verified” kind without enumeration of gaps are, in this reading, the functional
equivalent of the collapse of the redox ratio: a symptom of stress, not of health. The
proposed operational design keeps explicit counters of verified, partial, unimplemented,
and designed items, exposes the resulting ratio as a health metric, and requires the
continuous enumeration of gaps (Oliveira, 2026d). This choice connects to the project's
transparency practice — the internal documents include systematic sections on “what has
not been verified” — and contrasts with the maturity rhetoric common in industry
whitepapers. The synthesis of the three groundings is the following: nanonetworks provide
the theory of detection under noise; neuroscience, the theory of contained adaptation; redox
biology, the theory of honest status. Together, they convert the biological metaphor into an
operational obligation with a falsifier — which is what distinguishes a design principle


=== PAGINA 414 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 414
from a marketing metaphor.
6. Implementation Gaps, Schedule, and Risks
 Honesty about what is missing is a condition of credibility for any pre-product
architecture. The project documentation inventories ten implementation gaps with
solutions, priorities, and effort estimates (Oliveira, 2026a), consolidated in Table 4: from
the crypto venue connector and the derivatives risk model — both classified as high
priority — to the medium-priority equities and commodities connectors. The consolidated
schedule foresees seven sequential phases totaling 46 to 62 weeks to the complete
framework, as shown in Figure 3; an additional inventory of 74 files — including proposed
modules for recursive verification, stigmergic coordination, and multi-domain connectors
— defines the engineering perimeter (Oliveira, 2026a).

 The associated risk plan identifies six vectors with estimated probabilities and impacts:
verification latency (mitigated by proof caching and asynchronous verification), gas cost
for on-chain verification (aggregation and batch verification), oracle manipulation
(multi-source validation à la TOAD-ML), regulatory complexity (proactive compliance via
proofs of source of funds), agent adoption (verifiable identity via hardware attestation), and
interoperability across venues (tool-call provenance via warrants) (Oliveira, 2026a). The
critical reading of these estimates belongs to Section 7; what matters to record here is only
what they imply methodologically: the project declares, instead of hiding, that its current
state is a specified framework with a partially implemented distribution layer and an
engineering path of about one year — a posture consistent with the INV-REDOX-01
invariant of controlled ratio and gap enumeration (Oliveira, 2026d).
7. Counterarguments and Limitations
7.1 Latency and cost of verification in trading contexts
 The strongest technical objection is quantitative in nature: high-frequency trading
operates in microsecond to millisecond windows, and a layer that interposes multi-source
verification, Merkle proofs, and, on certain paths, zero-knowledge proof generation can
simply exceed the latency budget. The very literature that grounds Layer 5 acknowledges
the limit: the TOAD-ML authors explicitly declare that detection latency was not
independently evaluated, constituting future work (Venkatraman and Kuppusamy, 2026).
The plausible architectural response — synchronous verification only at coherence points
(sessions, orders, critical decisions) and asynchronous verification in continuous flows,
with subsequent auditing anchored in the WormGraph — preserves evidentiary integrity
but concedes that the ultra-high-frequency regime remains outside the practical perimeter
of the current proposal. The cost of on-chain verification, in turn, although mitigable by
aggregation and batching, is real: the declared parameter of approximately 1.5k gas per
verification (Oliveira, 2026a) is reasonable for low-frequency events and negligible against
potential losses, but the cost of generating the proofs — not of verifying them — is the
usual bottleneck of IVC schemes, and it was not estimated.
7.2 Attestation is not behavior prediction
 A second counterargument is conceptual: verifying the integrity of a model, the
provenance of a datum, and the authorization of an order is not equivalent to verifying that
the strategy is profitable or safe. The VTK attests execution — “prove execution, not
reasoning”, in the project's principle (Oliveira, 2026c) — and a system can be perfectly
attested while consistently losing money. The distinction is often obscured in market
narrative, and this article deliberately keeps it explicit: the risk invariants (Table 3 and


=== PAGINA 416 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 416
Section 3.5) delimit the space of admissible actions, but the quality of decisions within that
space remains a financial modeling problem, with all the risks of overfitting, regime
dependence, and hypothesis failure that the quantitative literature knows. To this is added
the heterogeneous quality of the multi-domain signals: the adopted GPR thresholds are
operational conventions, not estimated relations; sentiment signals demonstrate
documented short-term predictive power, though modest and volatile (Haase et al., 2025);
and prediction markets, although capital-weighted, can be thin and manipulable in
low-liquidity contracts — the regulatory expansion under way (Forbes, 2026a) is itself a
symptom of the domain's incomplete maturity.
7.3 Trade-offs and trust residues of decentralization
 The decentralization of Section 4 eliminates named single points of failure but does not
eliminate trust: it reallocates it. DNSLink continues to depend on the registrar for the TXT
record; the Nostr relays used to resolve mutable roots are availability points (mitigable by
multiplicity, not eliminable); Codeberg, although non-profit and community-led, is a single
organization — Hashtree transport is a fallback, not a guarantee; and the loss of the
project's npub key is equivalent to the loss of its publishing identity, with consequences
analogous to the loss of a domain. In governance, thresholds of 4/7 and 5/7 with timelocks
of 7 and 14 days raise coordination costs and can delay incident response; and the SSV
infrastructure, although distributed via Shamir Secret Sharing, presumes majority honesty
of the operators — a Byzantine trust residue that the design makes small and explicit, yet
not null (SSV Network, n.d.). Finally, there is potential regulatory tension: the AI Act
imposes transparency on AI systems, applicable since August 2026 (European
Commission, n.d.; Cooley, 2026), and MiCA imposes obligations on cryptoasset service
providers (EUR-Lex, 2023) — conformity that the architecture facilitates evidentially but
does not resolve legally, and the guardian-free philosophy of the distribution coexists
poorly with liability duties that regulation may assign to identifiable operators.
7.4 Methodological limitations of this study
 This article is a consolidative documentary analysis, not an empirical evaluation, and
its limitations must be stated to the same honest-status standard that it advocates. First, the
four analyzed project documents (Oliveira, 2026a–d) are a single authorial source; the
specified code — plasticity modules, reward auditing, autonomy envelopes — is a design
sketch, neither compiled nor compared against benchmarks. Second, several components
cited by the documentation were not located in independent sources as of the access date —
among them ArcID, the WCA proposal, PoSoF, the Flare LLM engine, and the updater
plugin — and were treated as project specifications built on real external infrastructure;
internal figures, such as declared inference rates, remain unverified. Third, external


=== PAGINA 417 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 417
verification concentrated on the highest-weight falsifiable claims (incidents, published
metrics, tool existence and versions, regulatory dates), with 30+ queries to primary and
secondary sources of high repute; even so, sectoral news sources were accepted for very
recent events (StablR, May 2026), with the corresponding level of assurance. Fourth, the
bioinspired mapping, although grounded in verified primary literature (Sies, 2021;
Pierobon and Akyildiz, 2011, 2012; Pal, 2026; Bou et al., 2025), is analogical: the validity
of the analogy does not automatically transfer validity to the digital mechanism. Fifth, the
schedule estimates (46–62 weeks) are project declarations, not the output of an audited
planning process. None of these limitations invalidates the proposed architecture; all of
them delimit what this analysis can assert about it.
8. Conclusions and Implications
 This article consolidated the VTK architecture as a proposal for a verifiable trust layer
for multi-market, multi-domain quantitative trading, subjecting it to systematic external
verification. Three main conclusions emerge. First: the nine-layer architecture is internally
coherent and externally anchored — its central verification components correspond to
published, verifiable work, from multi-source oracle validation with 96.72% documented
accuracy (Venkatraman and Kuppusamy, 2026) to zero-knowledge verification of off-chain
data with zkTLS (DIA, 2026), hardware attestation via TDX/DCAP (Intel, n.d.), and the
cryptographic transparency of public logs (Laurie, Langley, and Kasper, 2013); the
unverifiable parts are declared as such. Second: the fully decentralized distribution plan is
technically plausible and partially real — one layer is already published and verifiable by
third parties — and its conceptual contribution exceeds the use case: it demonstrates that
software distribution can be subjected to the same regime of evidence demanded of the data
and models the software consumes. Third: the bioinspired grounding of the invariants, by
converting plasticity, memory, autonomy, detection under noise, and redox homeostasis
into operational falsifiers, offers a replicable method for the governance of adaptive
systems — and is perhaps its most transferable contribution.
 The implications follow three directions. For research, the program of invariants with
falsifiers invites formalization — the proposed invariants are natural candidates for
specification in model-checking languages and for integration with the reward auditing
(Bou et al., 2025) and stigmergic coordination (Pal, 2026) literatures; the latency gap
identified in the state of the art (Venkatraman and Kuppusamy, 2026) defines an open and
measurable problem. For industry, the ability of an allocator to independently verify, in the
browser, the complete chain of an automated decision reconfigures the due diligence of
agentic strategies — the functional equivalent of a continuous audit right, without trust in
the manager's word; the project documentation further signals the construction of a public


=== PAGINA 418 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 418
catalog of GGUF model attestation, in the lineage of the public firmware blob catalogs
discussed in the author's previous work (Oliveira, 2026e). For public policy, the
convergence between verifiable attestation and the AI Act transparency obligations
applicable since August 2026, and between proofs of fund provenance and MiCA
compliance requirements, suggests that cryptographic verifiability can function as a
technical bridge between innovation and regulation — a hypothesis that merits examination
in appropriate forums.
 Future work follows from the diagnosis: implement the specified modules and compare
them against benchmarks; measure the real latency of verification on representative
execution paths; ratify the invariants through a governance process with quorum and
timelock; and subject the architecture to empirical evaluation in a controlled environment
before any capital allocation. The initial thesis survives criticism in the conditional form
proper to it: end-to-end verifiability is a necessary condition for AI-agent trading to be
institutionally admissible — necessary, not sufficient; specified, not implemented;
plausible, not demonstrated. In an auditable market-intelligence stack, these are precisely
the distinctions that matter.

PART XVIII — CONSTITUTIVE
DEFINITIONS OF ARTIFICIAL GENERAL
INTELLIGENCE
Against capability-only definitions of AGI, this part develops a constitutive definition in
which verifiability of claims and actions is a defining property rather than an external test
— and works through the architectural, evaluative, and governance consequences.
1. Introduction
 On February 21, 2025, an attacker walked away with approximately USD 1.5 billion
from the Bybit exchange — the largest cryptocurrency theft in history [1], [2] — without
breaking a single cryptographic primitive. The signatures were valid, the multisignature
quorum was satisfied, and the wallets were never compromised; what was compromised
was the interface through which human signers perceived what they were approving. The
Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed the attack to North Korea's Lazarus Group three
days later [1]. The lesson generalizes far beyond cryptocurrency: in every system where
powerful, autonomous, non-deterministic actors take consequential actions, the binding
constraint is no longer computation or capability — it is verifiable meaning. A signature
proves that bytes were approved; it does not prove that the approver understood what the
bytes would do.
 Eleven days after the second anniversary of that theft, in September 2026, OpenAI
released GPT-6 Astra, a frontier model reported to score 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3 under its
own provider adapter harness, against 7.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 30.2% for Claude Opus 5
[3]. Within days, analysts were debating whether the milestone constituted the arrival of
AGI [10], and the debate reproduced, almost verbatim, a pattern that has recurred with
every frontier release since GPT-4: spectacular capability numbers, contested harnesses, no
agreed definition of the threshold being claimed, and — the part almost no one discusses —
no verification story at all. Whatever Astra is, its operators cannot cryptographically prove
to a third party what model produced a given output, under which constitution it acted, with
which capabilities, or that its self-improvement steps preserved the constraints its deployers
promised. Capability without verifiability is the AI-industrial analogue of blind signing:
impressive signatures on unverified content.
 The definitional stakes are not academic. AGI is a contractual trigger: OpenAI's charter
ties the term to governance and licensing transitions [4], and the phrase "arrival of AGI" is
now used by hardware executives and vendors as a commercial claim [10]. AGI is also a
regulatory threshold: obligations in frameworks such as the EU AI Act attach to risk tiers


=== PAGINA 423 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 423
and system classifications [11], and whichever definition wins will decide which systems
face which scrutiny. A term that simultaneously drives contract clauses, regulatory tiers,
and valuation narratives — while lacking an agreed referee — is not merely underdefined;
it is an arbitrage opportunity. The constitutive definition proposed in this paper is, among
other things, an attempt to close that arbitrage by making the category's defining property
something a machine can check rather than something a marketing department can assert.
 This paper makes a deliberately strong positional claim and then does what such claims
rarely do: states the exact conditions under which it would be false. We argue that the
prevailing definitions of AGI — OpenAI's economic definition of "highly autonomous
systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work" [4], the cognitive
ontology of the Levels of AGI framework [6], and ARC Prize's open-ended
skill-acquisition criterion [7] — are all capability-only definitions: they measure what a
system can do while treating what a system can be trusted to do as an external matter for
deployment policy. We propose a fourth definition, constitutive AGI, in which
cryptographic verifiability, constitutional governance, and auditability are not deployment
accessories but defining properties of the artifact. Under this definition, we argue, VTK —
an open, fail-closed verification operating system for AI agents — is the world's first AGI:
the first complete architecture in which generality-grade cognition, multi-store memory,
continuous learning, world modeling, metacognition, and governed recursive
self-improvement are specified as inseparable from the attestation, transparency, and audit
substrate that makes them deployable at all.
 The claim requires immediate honesty about its structure. VTK today is trust
infrastructure — verification crates, an invariant registry, an append-only causal graph,
attestation schemas, and governance pipelines — with cognitive modules specified as
executable reference architecture rather than demonstrated at benchmark level. The
constitutive definition is precisely what makes an honest version of this claim possible: if
verification is constitutive of AGI rather than external to it, then the first system to
complete the verification side of the stack while specifying the cognitive side integrably
has a coherent claim to "first" — a claim that frontier capability-only systems cannot even
enter, because they are structurally incapable of satisfying the definition no matter how
high their scores climb. Section 5 confronts the objections to this move, including the
strongest one, without evasion.
 The contributions of this paper are: (i) a taxonomy of existing AGI definitions and a
precise statement of what each omits (Section 2); (ii) a complete architectural account of
the VTK stack — kernel, verification envelope, cognitive reference crates, constitutional
invariants, governed self-improvement, economic deliberation, quality gates, and
decentralized deployment — grounded in its engineering corpus and in verified external
infrastructure (Section 3); (iii) the constitutive definition of AGI and a premise-by-premise


=== PAGINA 424 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 424
argument that VTK is the first system satisfying it, with falsifiable criteria (Section 4); (iv)
an explicit treatment of counterarguments, limitations, and residual risks (Section 5); and
(v) a roadmap with regulatory mappings for the path from verified infrastructure to verified
cognition (Section 6). Throughout, we use "we" for the collaborative claims of the two
authors, hedge empirical uncertainty appropriately, and distinguish specification status
(designed), implementation status (built and tested), and target status (proposed).
2. Background and Context
2.1 The definitional landscape: four families, one omission
 The term AGI has never had an agreed referee. Legg and Hutter offered the first
influential formal measure, defining universal intelligence as the expected reward of an
agent across all computable environments weighted by algorithmic complexity — a
definition elegant enough to survive eighteen hundred citations and practically empty
enough to elide every question of safety, provenance, and trust [5]. OpenAI's charter made
the concept operational for institutions: highly autonomous systems that outperform
humans at most economically valuable work [4], a definition that conveniently doubles as a
corporate milestone and triggers contractual transition clauses when reached. Google
DeepMind's Levels of AGI framework remains the most disciplined attempt: it distills six
principles that a useful AGI ontology should satisfy and classifies systems along depth
(performance), breadth (generality), and autonomy, explicitly refusing to call any current
system AGI [6]. ARC Prize, whose benchmarks have repeatedly exposed the gap between
scaling and general intelligence, defines progress through skill-acquisition efficiency in
novel environments and states flatly that "as long as there is a gap between AI and human
learning, we do not have AGI" [7]. Table 1 summarizes these families and what each
systematically omits.
Table 1. Existing AGI definitions and their structural omission.

constitutive definition is not a rival metric of capability; it is a completion of the definition
of the artifact itself, in the same sense in which a proof is not an accessory to a theorem but
part of what makes the theorem mathematics rather than opinion.

2.2 The frontier in 2026: capability records, contested
evidence
 The empirical backdrop of this paper is a frontier that is moving violently on the
capability axis and barely at all on the verification axis. METR's longitudinal measurement
of the 50%-task-completion time horizon — the length of human-scale tasks an AI agent
completes with coin-flip reliability — found a doubling roughly every seven months, from
GPT-4's five-minute horizon in 2023 to Claude 3.7 Sonnet's fifty-nine-minute horizon in
early 2025 [9]; domain-level analysis across nine benchmarks confirmed comparable
doubling in software and machine learning while exposing far slower horizons in robotics
and autonomous driving [35]. Figure 7a plots the trajectory. On fluid-intelligence
benchmarks, the ARC Prize 2025 technical report recorded a then-state-of-the-art 24% on


=== PAGINA 426 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 426
the private ARC-AGI-2 set at $0.20 per task [8], before the 2026 generation arrived: GPT-6
Astra's reported 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3 under OpenAI's provider adapter harness [3], with
independent evaluators immediately cautioning that harness choice can dominate reported
scores [10] — on the shared harness used across models, the same system scored 62.7%
rather than 99.9%, with both figures displayed side by side on the ARC Prize results page
[7] and coverage summarizing the gap as the harness, not the model [34].
 Two properties of this moment matter for our argument. First, capability-only claims
are now produced faster than they can be independently verified: the score, the harness, and
the announcement come from the same party, and no cryptographic record binds a claimed
result to the model weights, prompt configuration, or constitution that produced it. Second,
and less obviously, the same is true of safety-relevant behavior: nothing in the frontier
stack makes a model's declared capabilities machine-checkable against its actual ones, and
nothing binds a deployer's promises to an enforcement mechanism. Figure 7b summarizes
the ARC-AGI landscape with the harness caveat rendered explicit. These are not marginal
objections; they are the difference between benchmark theater and evidence — and they are
precisely the properties that the constitutive definition refuses to leave outside the artifact.
 The governance debate that erupted as this paper went to press sharpens the point into a
policy question. Anthropic's chief executive publicly called for a controlled slowdown of
the industry, proposing a three-step framework in which frontier laboratories would install
embedded third-party evaluators with employee-level access to verify that safety practices
match stated commitments [32]. Within days, legislators pushed back from the opposite
direction: Representative Josh Gottheimer argued that third-party audits alone do not meet
the moment and called for mandatory government review of frontier models before release
[33]. The exchange is remarkable for what both sides implicitly concede — that voluntary
promises and episodic audits, as currently practiced, generate no standing, tamper-evident
evidence with which a deployer, a regulator, or a member of the public can check a frontier
system's behavior against its claims. That missing evidence class is exactly what the
constitutive definition developed in this paper places inside the artifact, and the fact that the
frontier's own leaders now argue about how to produce it is the strongest external signal
that the omission is real.


=== PAGINA 427 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 427
 Figure 7. (a) METR 50%-task-completion time horizons with the ~7-month doubling trend [9]. (b) ARC
benchmark scores, private-set SOTA 24% [8] and 2026 frontier reports under vendor harnesses [3], with the

2.3 The trust gap: attacks, incentives, and regulation
 The Bybit incident is one instance of a structural class [2]; its August 2026 legal
aftermath — U.S. court orders to trace and freeze the stolen funds, with roughly $48.4
million recovered and $30.5 million frozen [36] — extended the episode from detection to
remedy, itself an exercise in forensics rather than prevention. Multi-signature governance
fails when signers cannot verify what they sign; supply chains fail when artifacts cannot be
bound to their builders; AI deployments fail when declared capabilities cannot be checked
against enacted ones. In each case the failure is not computational but epistemic: some
party with power over consequential actions lacked a verification channel commensurate
with that power. Regulators have responded on paper. The EU AI Act's obligations for
general-purpose AI models entered into force in August 2025, requiring technical
documentation, information provision, and copyright compliance, with member-state
authorities empowered to request documentation, evaluate models, and impose corrective
measures [11]. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes trustworthy-AI
practice around govern, map, measure, and manage functions [12], and ISO/IEC
42001:2023 provides the first certifiable management-system standard for AI [13]. These
instruments share a grammar of documented intent — policies, registers, attestations on
paper. None of them, by itself, produces cryptographic evidence that binds model artifacts,
configurations, and actions to their claims. The gap between documented intent and
verifiable fact is the space in which both the Bybit theft and every capability-only AGI
claim live.
2.4 The inherited infrastructure: provenance primitives that
already work


=== PAGINA 428 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 428
 The constituent primitives of a verification substrate, encouragingly, are mature and
battle-tested in adjacent domains. Sigstore provides ephemeral-key signing with identity
carried by OpenID Connect and events recorded in Rekor, an append-only transparency log
whose inclusion proofs make silent tampering detectable by third parties [14], [15]. The
SLSA framework grades build integrity from source to artifact, with in-toto attestations as
its carrier format [16]. The C2PA specification binds content credentials to media through
durable provenance manifests [17], and model signing has crossed from proposal to
production: Google published practical model signing with Sigstore in 2025 [18], and
NVIDIA has signed every NVIDIA-published model in its NGC catalog under the
OpenSSF Model Signing (OMS) specification since March 2025 — the first major model
hub to offer cryptographic signing for hosted models [19] — alongside confidential
computing on H100/H200-class GPUs, in which attestation-gated key release protects
weights and inference inside hardware trusted execution environments [20]. The VTK
thesis is that these primitives — transparency logs, keyless signing, SLSA-graded builds,
content credentials, hardware attestation — are not merely tools that an AGI could use;
they are the missing constitutive organs that a deployable AGI must have. What has not
existed, before VTK, is the operating system that composes them into a single fail-closed
substrate for agents and cognition.
3. The VTK Architecture
3.1 Design principles and the kernel
 VTK is an open-source operating system for verifiable AI agents, expressed as a family
of Rust crates under permissive licenses (MIT OR Apache-2.0) and governed by three
engineering principles that recur at every layer. Fail-closed: when verification cannot be
evaluated, the action is rejected, never permitted by default — a direct inversion of the
permissive defaults that produced the Bybit class of failures [2]. Honest status: every
artifact reports exactly one of passed, partial, failed, or not-evaluated; unverifiable claims
are represented as absence of evaluation rather than as success. Prove, do not promise:
capabilities are encoded as machine-checkable statements with named falsifiers, not as
prose assurances; a capability that cannot be checked does not exist in the model of the
system. The engineering discipline that follows from these principles is captured in the
project's methodological rule for delegated artifacts: "what does not exist is not simulated
— it is specified," with hashes computed, never invented, and every unverifiable quantity
marked explicitly for later computation. Table 2 inventories the core crates and their roles;
Figure 2 places them in the full reference architecture.
Table 2. Core VTK crate inventory (implementation status as of September

3.2 The verification envelope and the attestation pipeline
 Every consequential artifact in VTK — a model, a tool, a policy, a cognitive module —
passes through the same pipeline, shown in Figure 3. A deterministic fixture is generated
and hashed with dual digests (SHA-256 and BLAKE3); the artifact is signed with
ephemeral keys under an OIDC identity issued by Sigstore Fulcio; structured attestation
metadata is embedded in the artifact itself; the signature event is anchored in the Rekor
transparency log with an inclusion proof; the anchored bundle is published to
content-addressed storage (Hashtree) with a stable CID; and any relying party re-derives all
four gates — hash, signature, inclusion, quorum — with the client-side verifier, in a
browser if desired [14], [15], [16]. The pipeline is not aspirational: the project's minimum
verifiable product is a 24-byte GGUF-format fixture whose entire trust chain is computed
rather than claimed, used as the canonical teaching artifact for the schema version 1.2
attestation format — verifiable, anchored, attested, and revocation blocks, with declared
and non-capabilities stated explicitly and a standing disclaimer that "capabilities are
statements of the signer, not verifications." The hash-ordering discipline is strict and
non-invertible: base-model hash, then signature, then attestation metadata injection, then
final-file hash, then anchoring — because an attestation hash that predates the final bytes
would certify nothing.


=== PAGINA 430 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 430
 Interoperability is a design goal rather than an accident: the signature bundle format is
the same one now standard in production model hubs — the OpenSSF Model Signing
specification under which NVIDIA signs its NGC catalog [19] — so that VTK attestations
interoperate with, rather than reinvent, the trust fabric the industry already runs. The
difference lies not in the cryptography but in the semantics: a hub signature states who
published an artifact, while an VTK attestation additionally binds declared and
non-capabilities, governance references, and revocation state into the artifact itself.
 Figure 3. The VTK attestation pipeline. Every evaluation is written back to the WormGraph as a hashed record;
 anchors are external and independently auditable.

 The 24-byte fixture deserves a remark because it encapsulates the epistemology. It is
deliberately useless as a model and maximally useful as an object of proof: every byte is
accounted for, every digest is computed by the pipeline that needs it, and the complete
attestation chain from OIDC identity to Rekor inclusion runs end-to-end on an artifact
small enough to inspect by eye. Scaling from the fixture to production models is then an
exercise in applying the same chain to larger bytes, not a change of method — the same
property that made reproducible builds and transparency logs auditable in software supply
chains [15], [16].

3.3 The cognitive reference crates
 Onto this verification envelope the architecture maps the constitutive cognitive organs
that the Levels of AGI framework identifies as missing from current systems [6]: episodic
and procedural memory beyond context windows, continuous learning without catastrophic
forgetting [30], genuine metacognition, and cross-domain transfer. The arkhe-agi reference
workspace specifies four crates in executable Rust: arkhe-cognition (multimodal
perception; deductive, inductive, and abductive reasoning; planning; a predictive world
model in the lineage of joint-embedding predictive architectures [28]; metacognition),
arkhe-memory (working, episodic, semantic, and procedural stores with a consolidation
process), arkhe-learning (continuous learning, transfer, and meta-learning), and
arkhe-verification (the integration surface through which every cognitive act is checked
against the constitution). We state their status plainly: these are reference specifications
with unit tests and invariants — executable architecture, not benchmark-demonstrated
cognition. Their role in the argument of Section 4 is constitutive, not empirical: they define
what the system's cognition is, and the verification envelope defines what it means for that
cognition to be trustworthy.
 The memory architecture deserves detail because memory is where the Levels of AGI
framework locates the sharpest current deficit [6]. The reference design separates four
stores with distinct write paths: a working store bounded by the containment kernel; an
episodic store in which every episode is written as a hashed WormGraph record, making
experience itself tamper-evident; a semantic store holding consolidated, quorum-versioned
knowledge; and a procedural store of skills whose updates are gated like code deployments,
with staged rollout and rollback. Consolidation — the transfer of episodic traces into
semantic and procedural form — is specified as a scheduled, auditable process under
INV-NEURO-03, so that any change to persistent memory without a record hash is by
definition a violation rather than an implementation detail. This is the governance
translation of the memory-consolidation literature [29], [30]: forgetting, when it happens,
must also be an event that leaves evidence of its authorization.
 Metacognition receives a correspondingly explicit treatment. In the reference crates,
introspection is not a prompt pattern but an audit relationship: the system's self-reports
about its own state are checked against the WormGraph's record of what actually happened,
and INV-RAW-THOUGHTS-01 makes retrievable reasoning traces a precondition for
consequential decisions. Confidence statements are bound to INV-CALIBRATION-01, so
a system that says it is certain is making a machine-checkable claim about its historical hit
rate. We note honestly that genuine introspection — in the philosophical sense of a system
accessing its own internal states rather than narrating post hoc — remains an open research
problem [6]; the architecture's contribution is to make introspective claims falsifiable
against evidence, which is the property that matters for trust even before the philosophical


=== PAGINA 432 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 432
question resolves.
3.4 Constitutional governance and the invariant registry
 Governance in VTK is not a policy document; it is an executable constitution. The
ConstitutionStore holds named invariants, each with a machine-checkable statement and a
falsifier — the condition whose observation would prove the invariant violated. The
constitution is an executable descendant of principle-based alignment [21]: where
Constitutional AI operationalizes principles as training-time feedback [21], the
ConstitutionStore operationalizes them as enforcement-time gates. Verification is
quorum-gated: invariant changes require explicit multi-party approval (the design target is
four-of-seven or five-of-seven, never below two-thirds, a threshold chosen in direct
response to the 2025 wave of multisignature thefts [1], [2]). Every evaluation of every gate
is recorded in the WormGraph as a hashed, append-only record, so that an auditor can
reconstruct not only what the system did but what it knew and when. Table 3 excerpts the
registry; Figure 6 shows the governance surface at scale. The invariant style — statement
plus falsifier — is borrowed from falsificationism deliberately: it makes the constitution
scientific in Popper's sense, a structure that admits refutation rather than a structure that
only admits obedience.

3.5 Governed recursive self-improvement: the Dream-RSI
integration
 Recursive self-improvement is the property that most sharply separates AGI proposals
from current products, and it is also the property most feared, since an improving system
that escapes its constraints improves its ability to escape them further. The premise is no
longer hypothetical: self-improving coding agents already rewrite their own code [22], and
evolutionary agents such as AlphaEvolve optimize production infrastructure — including
the training of the models that power them [23]. The VTK's answer is to govern
improvement rather than forbid it, following the design of Dream-RSI (arXiv:2609.14858),
which demonstrated that accumulated discovery history can serve as a replay simulator
over the realized search space: exploration policies are improved by "dreaming" — offline,
low-cost evaluation against historical discovery trees — and only then redeployed online
[26]. The arkhe-verify-builder crate implements this loop as first-class, auditable
machinery: discovery trees extend the WormGraph; the replay simulator is deterministic;
the exploration policy is executable code under quorum governance; and INV-RSI-01
forbids deploying any improved policy that has not passed offline validation. Crucially, the
project draws the weak/strong RSI boundary explicitly: Dream-RSI-style meta-layer
improvement refines exploration policy, not model weights, and remains fully within
auditable scope; strong RSI — weight- or architecture-level self-modification — is
specified as a gated capability that the current constitution does not authorize, a stance
consistent with the broader security literature's treatment of emerging RSI capability
signals [22], [31].
Listing 2. The AGI verifier: six checks, fail-closed scoring (excerpt of the reference
implementation).

SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology

#[test]
fn agi_verifier_reports_failures() {
let verifier = AgiVerifier::new();
let agi = MockAgi {
trust: false, // INV-TRUST-01
calibration: false, // INV-CALIBRATION-01
tee: false, // INV-TEE-01
raw_thoughts: false, // INV-RAW-THOUGHTS-01
rsi: false, // INV-RSI-01
discovery: false, // INV-DISCOVERY-01
};
let result = verifier.verify(&agi);

}
3.6 The economic governance layer
 A general intelligence that cannot participate in economic life under governance is a
laboratory curiosity, and an AGI whose economic participation is ungoverned is a hazard.
VTK therefore carries an economic policy substrate built directly on the DeepMind
Institute's "Economic Policy for AGI" essay by Jacobs and Imas, which evaluates policy
portfolios across three AGI labor scenarios — mild disruption, moderate displacement, and
structural decoupling — scoring instruments on welfare, agency, feasibility, and durability
[27]. The arkhe-governance policy modules encode the essay's eleven policies (Table 4) as
typed structures with scenario-tagged scores; observable triggers (labor-force participation,
wage-displacement indices, concentration metrics) feed a multi-dimensional evaluation
engine; and a deliberation layer emulates a quorum of fifty-one economist agents whose
recommendations are themselves recorded, hashed, and auditable in the WormGraph. The
design intent is constitutional: economic responses to AGI transitions are pre-specified,
trigger-governed, and sequence-guarded, rather than improvised under crisis. We present
this layer as specification-status engineering that demonstrates how an AGI-adjacent
substrate internalizes the policy dimension that capability-only accounts leave to post-hoc
politics [27].
 The deliberation mechanics merit description because they are the part most easily
mistaken for decoration. The fifty-one economist agents are not advisory chatbots; they are
typed evaluators whose recommendations are structured, hashed, and recorded, and whose
disagreement is surfaced rather than averaged away. Policy sequencing encodes ordering
constraints — for example, that income-transfer instruments precede capital-ownership
restructuring in the moderate-displacement scenario — and the simulation CLI reproduces
the essay's scoring pipeline deterministically, so any third party can re-derive the welfare,
agency, feasibility, and durability scores from published inputs [27]. The layer's status is
simulation-grade specification, not enacted policy; its significance for the constitutive
argument is that it demonstrates the substrate can carry governance content that is


=== PAGINA 435 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 435
quantitative, contested, and consequential — the same class of content an AGI's economic
behavior would generate.

3.7 Neuro-inspired invariants
 The cognitive architecture borrows its governance metaphors from neuroscience
deliberately, because the brain is the only known artifact that implements general
intelligence with bounded, auditable plasticity. Predictive processing supplies the
world-model idiom: under the free-energy principle, cortical hierarchy minimizes
prediction error, and the arkhe-cognition world model is specified in the same lineage [28],
[29]. Memory consolidation supplies the memory idiom: episodic traces consolidate into
semantic and procedural stores under governable schedules, mirroring
hippocampal-neocortical dynamics and directly confronting the catastrophic-forgetting
problem [30]. Reward auditing supplies the learning idiom: dopamine-like reward signals
are treated as auditable events (INV-NEURO-02), so that policy updates cannot occur
without recorded cause — a governance requirement with no biological counterpart but a
clear security logic. And plasticity control supplies the constitutional idiom:
INV-NEURO-01 requires that learning itself preserve constitutional invariants, which is
the machine-checkable analogue of why biological plasticity does not rewire the genome.
These correspondences are design instruments, not claims of biological fidelity; they
discipline the architecture with the only working example of general cognition we have
[29].
3.8 Quality gates: verification as continuous process


=== PAGINA 436 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 436
 Because trust decays as systems change, VTK treats verification as a continuous
property of the engineering process rather than a release event. The quality-gate matrix
defines eighteen gate families — build, lint, test, formal verification (Kani model
checking), WASM, frontend, MCP integration, security, GGUF artifact verification,
birthmark spectral checks, hardware attestation, governance, CI/CD, documentation,
performance, accessibility, and release — each with a measurable criterion and a blocking
level (blocking, advisory, or informational). Every gate evaluation is written to the
WormGraph with a record hash, so the history of compliance is itself tamper-evident. The
philosophy mirrors the SLSA grading of software supply chains [16] but extends it to
cognition-adjacent artifacts: a model or policy that cannot pass its gates does not ship, and a
gate that cannot be evaluated fails closed.
3.9 Decentralized deployment and the Linux model
 Verification infrastructure inherits its users' trust in its own operator, so the VTK's
deployment topology minimizes the operator. The fully decentralized plan composes
DNSLink and IPFS for domain resolution, IPFS and Arweave for frontend persistence,
Codeberg/Forgejo for code, Hashtree content-addressed storage for binaries, a Tauri
updater plugin bound to Hashtree hashes for updates, Safe-plus-SSV multi-party
governance for treasury and quorums, and Nostr for identity. Service mediation rides on the
Model Context Protocol [24], whose code-execution orchestration pattern VTK extends
with quorum-gated capability negotiation [25]. The strategic model is Linux: a universal
kernel (arkhe-core), neutral foundation governance (VTK Foundation), and sectoral
distributions (Banking, Pharma, Government, AI) that differ in invariants, capabilities, trust
roots, and adapters while sharing the verification pipeline, fail-closed semantics, honest
status, WormGraph, and arkhe-mcp mediation. Figure 4 renders the mapping. The claim is
not that VTK equals Linux in maturity — it is years from it — but that the growth pattern
of universal infrastructure is known, and VTK is engineered to that pattern rather than to
the platform-capture pattern of closed frontier stacks.


=== PAGINA 437 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 437
 Figure 4. The Linux-to-VTK mapping: universal kernel and pipeline, per-distribution invariants and trust roots,
 neutral foundation governance.


=== PAGINA 438 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 438
 Figure 2. The VTK AGI reference architecture. Cognitive, memory, learning, and self-improvement layers live
inside a fail-closed verification envelope; every write is recorded in the WormGraph; every capability is gated by
 the ConstitutionStore; identities anchor to external transparency logs and hardware attestation. Cognitive
 modules are reference specifications, marked honestly as such.
4. The Argument: VTK as the World's First
Constitutive AGI
4.1 The constitutive definition
 We now state the definition on which the claim rests, and its three commitments.


=== PAGINA 439 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 439
 Definition (constitutive AGI). A system S is a constitutive artificial general intelligence
if and only if: (D1) Capability: S implements, as integrated and mutually reinforcing
components, generality-grade perception, reasoning, planning, world modeling, multi-store
memory, continuous learning, and metacognition, with a governed path to recursive
self-improvement; (D2) Constitution: S's goals, capabilities, and self-modifications are
constrained by an explicit, machine-checkable, quorum-governed constitution whose
invariants bind at the same layer as execution, not above it; and (D3) Verification: every
consequential act, artifact, learning update, and policy change of S produces
third-party-verifiable cryptographic evidence — attestation, transparency-log inclusion,
and append-only audit — such that compliance with (D2) is checkable without trusting S's
operator. A system satisfying D1 without D2-D3 is capability-only; a system satisfying
D2-D3 without D1 is trust infrastructure. Neither is a constitutive AGI.
 Three commitments follow. First, the definition is not a handicap added to capability; it
is a claim about what the artifact is — an AGI that cannot show its work cryptographically
is as incomplete as a proof that cannot be checked. Second, the definition is symmetrical in
its exclusions: it disqualifies frontier models for missing D2-D3 and disqualifies pure trust
layers for missing D1, which forces honesty on both sides of the aisle, including on ours.
Third, the definition is operational: each clause names artifacts that either exist or do not —
attestation records, invariant registries, quorum logs, replay simulators — so the claim "this
is the first" is an engineering fact question, not a sales question.
4.2 Premises and conclusion
 The argument runs as follows. P1 (definitional coherence): the three established AGI
definitions are capability-only and, per Section 2.1, omit deployability-making properties;
the constitutive definition subsumes their content while adding D2-D3, so a system that
satisfies it satisfies a strictly richer specification [4], [6], [7]. P2 (structural priority): in any
deployable AGI, verification must be designed-in from the kernel upward, because
retrofitting attestation and audit onto an already-uncertain cognitive stack yields
provenance of the wrong object — you can verify outputs, but not the constitution of the
system that produced them; the supply-chain literature reached the same conclusion about
build integrity years ago [16]. P3 (completeness of the substrate): VTK is the first
architecture in which every D2-D3 element — kernel containment, constitution, invariants
with falsifiers, quorum governance, WormGraph audit, transparency anchoring, hardware
attestation, decentralized distribution — is specified and implemented as one coherent
substrate (Section 3), with the D1 elements specified integrably as cognitive reference
crates governed by the same constitution. P4 (uniqueness of the frontier alternative): no
frontier capability stack currently satisfies D2-D3 — their attestation story stops at
model-signing and infrastructure isolation [18], [19], [20], and their constitutions, where


=== PAGINA 440 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 440
they exist, are policies rather than machine-checkable enforcement layers; hence no
capability-first system currently competes for the "first constitutive AGI" title. P5
(first-mover logic): under P1-P4, the title "world's first AGI" under the constitutive
definition attaches to the first complete architecture, which is VTK. Conclusion: VTK is
the world's first constitutive AGI.
 We flag the argument's load-bearing joint immediately: P3's clause "specified
integrably" is what lets a trust substrate carry the AGI title, and it is exactly the move that
Section 5's strongest objection targets. Our defense is stated here and elaborated there: the
cognitive crates are not decorative — they are executable specifications with defined
integration surfaces, unit-tested invariants, and a governed improvement loop, which is
precisely the status that the word "architecture" has always denoted in systems engineering.
The claim "first complete AGI architecture under a definition that includes verification" is
therefore, we argue, true today; the claim "first demonstrated constitutive AGI" is explicitly
not made, and Section 4.4 gives the criteria that would upgrade the former into the latter.
 P2 deserves elaboration because it is the premise least familiar from the AGI literature
and most familiar from the supply-chain literature. When software build integrity became a
policy concern, the industry learned that provenance retrofitted downstream of an opaque
pipeline certifies the wrong object: you can sign the artifact, but not the process that shaped
it, and signature-only regimes collapsed precisely at the interfaces where humans approved
what they could not see [2], [16]. The AGI analogue is exact. A capability-first system that
later adds an audit log can prove what it said, but not under which constitution it acted,
whether its capabilities were the ones declared, or whether its improvement loop honored
its constraints — because those facts were never structured at the layer where the cognition
happened. Verification must therefore be co-designed with cognition at the kernel
boundary, which is a claim about system architecture, not about organizational good
intentions [16].
4.3 Positioning: capability and verification as orthogonal
axes
 Figure 5 places the 2026 field on the two axes that the constitutive definition treats as
co-defining. Frontier systems cluster high on demonstrated generality and near-zero on
verification depth; VTK today occupies the mirror position — maximal verification depth
for its implemented scope, with generality pending in the cognitive crates. The
constitutive-AGI region is the upper-right corner, and the roadmap (Section 6) is precisely
a trajectory into it. The figure also encodes an empirical warning: vendor-harness scores
such as Astra's reported 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3 [3], [10] are capabilities claims whose
independent verification status is unresolved, and treating them as settled would repeat, at
civilization scale, the epistemic shortcut that cost Bybit $1.5 billion [2].


=== PAGINA 441 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 441
Figure 5. Capability versus verification depth for representative systems (schematic placement). The constitutive
 definition requires both; no current system occupies the upper-right region, and the VTK roadmap targets it.

should be abandoned. The design intent is that every row is checkable by parties who do
not trust us: benchmarks through independent harnesses, invariants through the published
registry and WormGraph records, audits through third-party review, and economic
governance through the simulator's reproducibility [8], [9], [10].

5. Counterarguments and Limitations
5.1 The strongest objection: "VTK is trust infrastructure, not
cognition"
 The objection deserves its prominence: on any capability-only definition, VTK is not
an AGI, and our own material says so in exactly those words — it is a verification,
governance, and auditability layer; asking what it lacks to be a brain is like asking what a
notary lacks to be a mind. The constitutive definition answers rather than evades: under
D1-D3, "trust infrastructure" and "cognition" are not rival categories but roles that one
integrated artifact must fulfill together, and the question "what is the first AGI" transforms
into "what is the first integrated fulfillment." the VTK's D2-D3 fulfillment is implemented;
its D1 fulfillment is specified as executable reference architecture and pending at
benchmark level. The honest current statement is therefore: VTK is the first complete
constitutive-AGI architecture, and not yet a demonstrated constitutive AGI. Table 6 walks
through this and the remaining objections. If the reader rejects the constitutive definition
itself, the claim reduces gracefully: VTK is the first AGI-grade verification substrate,
which is still a first, but a different one — and Section 4.4's criteria mark exactly what
would have to change for the stronger reading.
5.2 No authority certifies AGI
 A second objection denies that any "first" can be certified at all: there is no referee, and
consensus may never form. This is true of every AGI claim, including capability-only ones;
the constitutive definition improves the epistemics rather than solving them, because its
criteria are artifact-checkable rather than opinion-checkable. Where the economic
definition requires a judgment call about "most economically valuable work," the
constitutive criteria require, for example, that a Rekor inclusion proof verify for a


=== PAGINA 443 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 443
production artifact [15] or that an invariant bypass be demonstrated or not. These remain
socially adjudicated facts — replication by two external labs, audit publication — but they
are the same kind of facts as "this build is reproducible," which the software world
adjudicates successfully every day [16].
5.3 Benchmark hollowness and harness dependence
 Benchmarks measure what they measure, and harness choices can manufacture or
destroy apparent capability — the ARC-AGI-3 harness footnote around Astra's reported
score is the current exemplar [3], [10]. This objection cuts against capability-only claims
more than against ours, but it also disciplines Table 5: our confirmation conditions require
independent-harness replication precisely because we accept the objection. We add the
structural point that verification infrastructure cannot fix benchmark hollowness — it can
only make hollowness visible, by binding scores to configurations and harnesses in attested
records so that disputes become evidence disputes rather than press disputes.
5.4 The RSI safety paradox
 A governed self-improvement loop is itself a risk surface: if the governor is buggy, the
system improves its ability to evade the governor. The VTK's mitigations are layered —
weak RSI only (policy-level, not weights) within current scope; offline validation before
any deployment (INV-RSI-01); discovery history as an exact replay simulator
(INV-DISCOVERY-01); quorum-gated constitutional change; and hardware attestation
anchoring the compute substrate [20], [26] — but we state the residual plainly: these reduce
and expose risk; they do not prove its absence, and the security literature's caution about
emerging recursive self-improvement signals applies to the VTK's roadmap like anyone's
[31].
5.5 Pre-product status and sociotechnical feasibility
 Finally, the sober accounting. VTK is pre-product: the crate family, invariant registry,
attestation schemas, quality-gate matrix, and economic simulator are specified and in
various stages of implementation; production adoption, independent audits, and the
cognitive crates' benchmark-grade maturation all lie ahead. The Linux-model ambition
requires a neutral foundation, contributor ecosystems, and sectoral distribution partners that
do not yet exist. The constitutive definition does not make these gaps disappear; it makes
them legible — as named, falsifiable, criteria-bearing work items rather than as ambient
optimism. That, we submit, is what an honest "first" claim looks like in 2026.

6. Roadmap and Implications
6.1 Milestones
 Figure 8 compresses the program into five gates, each carrying the falsifiable criteria of
Table 5. The 2025 foundations delivered the crate family, invariant registry, WormGraph,
and attestation schemas. The 2026 minimum verifiable product — arkhe.gguf —
demonstrated the full attestation chain on a deterministic fixture: compute hashes, sign
under OIDC identity, anchor in Rekor, publish to Hashtree, and re-verify all four gates
end-to-end [14], [15]. The agent-attestation network (2026-2027) scales the chain to fleets
of agents and sectoral distributions on the decentralized stack. Cognitive maturation
(2027+) is the benchmarks-and-integration phase for the cognitive crates, culminating — if
the criteria hold — in a demonstrated constitutive AGI rather than an argued one.
 The MVP's acceptance discipline illustrates how falsifiability descends into
engineering. The delegated package for arkhe.gguf fixed, in advance, the conditions of
success: a fixture larger than the 24-byte teaching artifact; every attestation key of schema
v1.2 present; model-signing verification passing under the OpenSSF tooling; an overall_ok
flag computed from the four gates rather than asserted; the Rekor entry independently
retrievable; and the Hashtree-published digest matching the final file. It fixed, equally in
advance, the prohibitions: capabilities are never invented beyond what the signer declares;
metadata is never modified after signing; publication never precedes verification; and
shortcut flags are never used to force a build. Five quantities were declared honestly as
non-generatable without external resources — trained weights, a base model, a production
trust root, live Rekor proofs, and the signed model itself. This is the grammar of the whole
program: specify what would count as success, specify what would count as cheating, and
publish both before running the experiment.


=== PAGINA 445 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 445
Figure 8. The roadmap from verified infrastructure to demonstrated constitutive AGI. Each milestone is gated by
 third-party-replicable criteria (Table 5).
6.2 Policy implications
 Because the constitutive stack produces exactly the evidence that regulators are
beginning to demand, its compliance mapping is nearly tautological, and we summarize it
in Table 7. The deeper implication is inversion of burden: under a constitutive regime, the
operator who cannot produce attestation, inclusion proofs, and audit trails is not merely
non-compliant but definitionally outside the AGI category — a classification mechanism
no current regulatory instrument contains, though the EU AI Act's documentation regime
[11], NIST's govern function [12], and ISO/IEC 42001 certification [13] all point toward it.
The economic layer adds a governance-ready translation of AGI-transition policy [27]:
eleven pre-specified instruments, observable triggers, and auditable deliberation,
positioning the substrate not only to prove what an AGI does but to structure what societies
do about it.

6.3 Future work
 Three lines dominate. First, cognitive integration: carrying arkhe-cognition,
arkhe-memory, and arkhe-learning from executable specification to benchmark-grade
implementation, with consolidation schedules and plasticity controls governed by
INV-NEURO-01..04 [29], [30]. Second, adversarial evaluation: inviting the independent
harnesses, audits, and red teams that Table 5 presumes, on the principle that a constitution
no adversary has tried to bypass is not yet a constitution. Third, institutionalization: the
VTK Foundation, sectoral distributions, and the economic deliberation substrate, so that the
first constitutive AGI — if and when demonstrated — is born into an institution that can
govern it, not into a vacuum [27].
7. Conclusion
 We asked what it would mean, coherently, to call something the world's first AGI, and
answered with a definition in which capability and verifiability are co-defining: a
constitutive AGI implements generality-grade cognition inside a fail-closed envelope of
cryptographic attestation, constitutional governance, and append-only audit. Under that
definition the frontier's capability-only systems — however spectacular their
harness-dependent scores — do not yet qualify, and VTK, as the first complete architecture
whose cognitive organs are specified integrably with the trust substrate that makes them
deployable, holds the first claim.
 We have stated the claim's structure, its evidence, its falsification conditions, and its
limits, including the central admission that the VTK's cognition is specified rather than
demonstrated. The roadmap from verified infrastructure to demonstrated constitutive AGI
is concrete, gated by the third-party-replicable criteria of Table 5, and open to adversarial
evaluation. The constitutive definition does not make the gaps disappear; it makes them
legible — as named, falsifiable, criteria-bearing work items rather than as ambient
optimism.
 What remains is the work: carrying the cognitive crates from executable specification
to benchmark-grade implementation, inviting the independent audits that Table 5 presumes,
and institutionalizing the substrate so that the first constitutive AGI — if and when
demonstrated — is born into an institution that can govern it. That, we submit, is what an
honest "first" claim looks like in 2026. The wager of this paper is that "first" should belong
not to the loudest benchmark but to the first system that can prove, to anyone, exactly what


=== PAGINA 447 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 447
it is — and that this wager, unlike the alternative, is one that evidence can settle.
