PART XIX — SOVEREIGN COMPUTE: A
NATIONAL REPAIRABLE SMARTPHONE
PROGRAM
This part applies the verification-first governance (VFG) discipline to sovereign, repairable
smartphone programs. It examines the LibrePhone program, launched by the Free Software
Foundation in October 2025 to replace the proprietary binary blobs that dominate mobile
firmware — including Qualcomm's WPSS wireless subsystem and its CopyEngine DMA
controller — through clean-room reproduction grounded in the Sega v. Accolade
precedent. The analysis maps a structural isomorphism between LibrePhone's public blob
catalog and the model-attestation catalogs required for verifiable AI agents under the
Verifiable Trust Kernel (VTK), along four dimensions: the isomorphic trust deficit, the
parallel methods, auditable public catalogs, and license and governance alignment. Three
concrete applications with prioritized recommendations are derived; counterarguments —
techno-economic viability, the gap between verifying code and verifying stochastic
behavior, and the freedom-versus-security tension — are weighed; and the methodological
limitations of the documentary analysis are stated. Throughout, the framework's demand is
the same: convert trust into verifiable evidence and attach falsifiers to each claim.
1. Introduction
 On March 29, 2024, security engineers identified in xz-utils, a compression library
present in thousands of Linux distributions, a backdoor deliberately inserted into its build
process — CVE-2024-3094, classified with the maximum severity score (NVD, 2024).
Less than a year later, on February 21, 2025, the exchange Bybit suffered the largest
cryptocurrency theft in history, on the order of US$1.5 billion, attributed by the FBI to
state-sponsored actors of North Korea (FBI, 2025). Although the two incidents belong to
distinct domains, they illuminate the same structural problem: in complex digital
environments, trust is frequently granted without evidence — to an unknown maintainer, to
a binary without source code, to an interface that simply displays an address. When such
blind trust is exploited, there is no verification path that would allow the user — or even the
institution — to detect the divergence between what a system declares it does and what it
actually does.
 The scale of the problem is difficult to overstate. Sector estimates indicate about 3.9
billion active Android devices worldwide, corresponding to approximately 73% of the
mobile operating system market at the end of 2025 (Statista, 2026). Each of these devices
carries, in addition to its open-source core, dozens to hundreds of binary blobs — libraries
and firmware compiled without associated source code — that execute in privileged


=== PAGINA 451 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 451
contexts: the modem, signal processors, wireless subsystems, memory controllers
(LineageOS, 2026). The typical user cannot study these components, cannot modify them
and, in many cases, cannot even know with precision what they do. In the terminology
developed in this part, this is a verifiability deficit in the physical substrate of personal
computing.
 The deficit, however, is not limited to firmware. The rise of AI agents — systems
based on large language models that operate with varying degrees of autonomy, invoking
tools and executing actions on behalf of users — reproduces, at another layer of the
computing stack, the same asymmetry: the user delegates authority to an artifact whose
behavior cannot be verified. Recent mitigation proposals concentrate on cryptographic
attestation mechanisms — immutable records of model identity and provenance, execution
confined within containment kernels, and verifiable audit trails — as in the Verifiable Trust
Kernel (VTK), a verifiable trust layer for AI agents described in the technical
documentation of the Safe Core project (Oliveira, 2026a). The parallel with the software
freedom agenda is no coincidence: both programs respond to the fundamental question of
how to ensure that a system does what it says it does, without depending on blind trust in a
vendor.
 This part examines that convergence hypothesis through a concrete case: the
LibrePhone project, announced by the Free Software Foundation (FSF) on October 14,
2025, as part of the celebrations of the foundation's fortieth anniversary (FSF, 2025a; FSF,
2025c). Led by developer Rob Savoye — a long-standing GNU project contributor, active
since the 1980s — LibrePhone is not yet another Android distribution: it is a long-term
program to understand, catalog and, through clean-room reverse engineering, replace the
proprietary components present in virtually all current mobile systems-on-chip (SoC) (FSF,
2025a; Savoye, 2026). The thesis defended here is that LibrePhone and the VTK are,
methodologically, two sides of the same coin: the first liberates the hardware from
proprietary blobs; the second liberates AI software from blind trust; and together they
suggest a complete digital sovereignty stack — from firmware to AI agent, everything
verifiable.
 The concept of digital sovereignty adopted here follows the formulation current in
European public policy studies: the capacity to act independently in the digital world, in
terms of both technological autonomy and normative control (EPRS, 2023). This part
deliberately operates on the individual and structural dimension of that capacity — what
might be called user sovereignty — and proposes that verifiability is its technical condition
of possibility: there is no effective exercise of control over what cannot be examined or
audited. In this sense, the part connects a tradition — the defense of the four software
freedoms (GNU, n.d.; Stallman, 2002) — to an emerging problem — the governance of AI
agents — through a structural analysis of their methods.


=== PAGINA 452 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 452
 The remainder of the text is organized as follows. Section 2 presents the foundations:
software freedom, the blob problem in Android, the precursors of LibrePhone, the project
itself, and the VTK. Section 3 develops the structural convergence analysis along four
dimensions. Section 4 derives concrete applications and strategic recommendations for the
VTK. Section 5 discusses counterarguments and limitations, including those of the method
adopted here. Section 6 concludes and points to implications and future work.
2. Foundations and Related Work
2.1 Software freedom and the four freedoms
 The tradition from which LibrePhone descends dates back to 1985, with the founding
of the Free Software Foundation by Richard Stallman, and to the formulation that a
program is free when it guarantees users four essential freedoms: to run the program as
they wish; to study how the program works and adapt it; to redistribute copies; and to
distribute modified versions (GNU, n.d.; Stallman, 2002). The central distinction is not one
of cost but of control: non-free software transfers to the vendor the prerogative of deciding
what the user may know and do. For four decades, the epicenter of this dispute was desktop
computers and servers — territory in which systems such as GNU/Linux achieved broad
functional coverage, albeit with non-negligible proprietary residues, especially in board and
peripheral firmware.
 When announcing LibrePhone, FSF executive director Zoë Kooyman summarized the
diagnosis motivating the expansion of the agenda to the mobile environment: forty years
after the founding, the initial focus on desktop and server systems remained unchanged
while computing migrated massively to phones — the primary computing device for most
people in the world (FSF, 2025a). The move is therefore a relocation of the classic freedom
agenda to the device that effectively concentrates contemporary digital life and that
remains, at the firmware level, largely inaccessible to user examination (FSF, 2025b).
2.2 The problem of binary blobs in Android devices
 The Android ecosystem illustrates the anatomy of the problem with precision. The core
of Android is the GNU/Linux kernel, distributed under the GPL-2.0 license, and much of
the platform is covered by permissive licenses; however, between the kernel and the
hardware resides a layer of software that manufacturers deliver only as binaries: modem,
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and image-processing firmware, drivers, and user-space libraries in
compiled form. The LineageOS project — the most widely adopted community Android
distribution — documents the standard industry procedure: the so-called proprietary blobs
are extracted from the device's factory images by means of utilities such as extract-files.sh,
which processes declared lists of proprietary files and copies them into the build tree


=== PAGINA 453 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 453
(LineageOS, 2026). In other words: even distributions called free incorporate, as raw
material, binaries whose provenance is the very proprietary stack they were meant to
replace.
 The technical and political consequence is twofold. Technically, these blobs execute in
privileged and frequently autonomous contexts — the modem decides with whom the radio
communicates; dedicated subsystems, such as Qualcomm's Wireless Processor SubSystem
(WPSS), carry their own firmware (wpss.b01 to wpss.b05 on recent platforms) and direct
memory access controllers, such as the CopyEngine, operating outside the kernel's
visibility (LibrePhone, 2026; Qualcomm, 2025). Politically, the formal freedom to compile
the upper stack coexists with the practical impossibility of auditing the lower stack — a
situation the FSF characterizes as the principal remaining locus of non-freedom in mobile
computing (FSF, 2025b). It is worth noting that technical standards for firmware resiliency,
such as NIST SP 800-193, assume precisely this scenario by requiring protection,
detection, and recovery mechanisms for firmware components — today, mostly opaque
(NIST, 2018).
2.3 Precursors: Replicant, LineageOS, and the state of
practice
 LibrePhone does not arise in a vacuum. Replicant, started in 2010, is the Android
distribution expressly dedicated to being totally free, replacing proprietary components
with its own implementations wherever possible (Replicant, 2026). Figure 3 situates these
and other relevant milestones on a timeline. Its trajectory, however, exposed the cost of the
approach: device support was restricted to a narrow set of handsets — precisely those
whose hardware admits blob substitution or abstention — and the pace of tracking platform
versions became chronically limited by dependence on volunteers. LineageOS, in turn,
adopted the opposite pragmatic stance: maximize device coverage and timeliness,
accepting the incorporation of blobs extracted from factory images (LineageOS, 2026).
Between these two strategies — purity with minimal coverage and maximal coverage with
minimal purity — lies the design space that LibrePhone proposes to attack from another
flank: rather than choosing between free and functional devices, to produce, through
reverse engineering, the free specifications and implementations that allow existing
distributions (LineageOS, Replicant, and others) to gradually reduce their dependence on
sourceless binaries (FSF, 2025a; Savoye, 2026).


=== PAGINA 454 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 454
Figure 3 — Timeline of the milestones relevant to the argument (1985–2026), the author's own elaboration based
 on the cited sources.
 This strategy has consolidated legal grounding. In the precedent Sega Enterprises Ltd.
v. Accolade, Inc. (977 F.2d 1510, U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, 1992), it was
established that software reverse engineering by disassembly, when performed to access
unprotected functional elements and enable interoperability, constitutes legitimate use (fair
use) under U.S. copyright law (Justia, 1992). This is exactly the legal regime on which
clean-room practice rests: one team analyzes the binary and produces a descriptive
specification; a separate team, without contact with the original code, implements from the
specification — reducing the risk of contamination by copying and, at the same time,
producing artifacts that Accolade-case doctrine tends to protect. It should be noted that the
extent of this regime varies by jurisdiction; the analysis developed here takes the U.S.
precedent as its documented reference, without claiming universal legal generalization.
2.4 The LibrePhone project: scope, method, and tools
 LibrePhone was publicly announced on October 14, 2025, as a partnership between the
FSF and Rob Savoye, in the context of the foundation's 40th anniversary and its leadership
transition (FSF, 2025a; FSF, 2025c). The project's website indicates that exploration of the
area had begun on August 11, 2025, and is explicit about scope: “not another Android
distribution, but a long-term effort to understand and reverse engineer the nonfree
components used in virtually all current SoCs” (FSF, 2025b; LibrePhone, 2026). The
declared objective is to develop free substitutes for binary blobs in the firmware of Android
devices, strengthening existing distributions — not competing with them. Table 1
summarizes the project's scope.
 The project's central instrument is a set of analysis and cataloging tools, published as
free software on Codeberg (Savoye, 2026). extractor.py imports into a database
information on all proprietary files and binary blobs present in the distributions' installation
images; import_dev.py processes specific devices; query_dev.py queries the database for
the location, function, and dependencies of each blob; and generator.py produces bindings
for Python or Postgres, allowing CSV export for external analysis (LibrePhone, 2026;


=== PAGINA 455 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 455
Savoye, 2026). The tools presuppose obtaining the LineageOS installation packages for the
devices of interest, and a top-level script, images_util.sh, automates batch processing of
multiple handsets (Savoye, 2026). In other words: LibrePhone's first deliverable is not a
free driver, but a structured, auditable inventory of opacity — the cartography of the
problem before its solution.
Table 1 — The LibrePhone (FSF) project in summary (the author's own
elaboration based on FSF, 2025a, 2025b; LibrePhone, 2026; Savoye, 2026).
Aspect
Description

with Rob Savoye, a GNU developer since the 1980s.
Focus
Binary blobs in the firmware of Android devices: SoCs, wireless subsystems (WPSS, ATH11k), DMA
controllers (CopyEngine).

Accolade, 977 F.2d 1510).

 The technical dimension of the research is documented on the project's website in
pages dedicated to concrete targets: the ATH11k firmware (Wi-Fi), the Wireless Processor
SubSystem — expressly described by the project as an object of study, with the variants
wpss.b01 to wpss.b05 cataloged — and the CopyEngine, a DMA controller of Qualcomm
subsystems (LibrePhone, 2026). Note the project's own methodological prudence:
preliminary assessments are qualified by the author — per Savoye's correspondence of
June 21, 2026, referenced on the site — as subject to revision, indicating a discipline of
analytical versioning uncommon in reverse engineering projects (LibrePhone, 2026).
2.5 The Verifiable Trust Kernel: a verifiable trust layer for AI
agents
 At the opposite end of the stack, the VTK is described in technical documentation as a
verifiable-trust operating system for AI agents, structured around three principal
mechanisms (Oliveira, 2026a). First, a containment kernel that executes the agent in an
isolated environment, limiting its action surface to declared operations. Second,
cryptographic attestation of models: each AI artifact (for example, a model in GGUF
format) receives a verifiable identity composed of a content hash, a digital signature, and
metadata of provenance and declared capabilities. Third, the WormGraph — an immutable
evidence graph based on Merkle trees (Merkle, 1987), with SHA-256 addressing, Ed25519
signatures, and periodic anchoring of roots in the Rekor public transparency log of the


=== PAGINA 456 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 456
Sigstore ecosystem (Sigstore, 2026) — which guarantees that any statement about the
agent's behavior can be independently re-verified.
 The project's motivation is documented in incident analyses and architecture decisions:
the Bybit case (blind signing of a US$1.5 billion transaction approved in an interface that
concealed the real destination address — FBI, 2025), along with episodes such as StablR (a
US$13.5 million payment authorized with a 1-of-3 quorum) and SUPERFORTUNE
(US$15.18 million diverted to a visually similar address), converge on the conclusion that
approval flows without independent verification produce catastrophic failures (Oliveira,
2026a). Hence architecture rule ADR-011: a minimum approval quorum of 4-of-7 or 5-of-7
(quorums below 2/3 prohibited) and separation between authority (ConstitutionStore,
which defines the operational constitution) and witness (multisig wallet integrations such as
Safe, which merely observe and execute) (Oliveira, 2026a). The project's motto — “prove,
don't promise” — condenses the same methodological wager this part identifies in
LibrePhone: replacing promises of trust with verifiable artifacts.
 As for license governance, the kernel's components described in the documentation —
the crates arkhe-core, arkhe-crypto, arkhe-governance, arkhe-evidence, arkhe-wormgraph,
and arkhe-verify-wasm, among others — adopt dual licensing under MIT OR Apache-2.0,
expressed in SPDX notation, with declared compatibility with the FSF's freedom
requirements (Oliveira, 2026a). This seemingly minor detail is structural for the argument
of this part: it is what makes the convergence with the FSF ecosystem technically viable
and legally clean, as discussed in Section 3.5.
3. Structural Convergence: A Comparative
Analysis
 This section develops the analytical core of the part. The comparison is not a rhetorical
analogy but a mapping of functional isomorphisms: in each dimension examined, both
projects face the same problem structure and produce solutions with the same logical form,
albeit over distinct technological substrates. Table 1 summarizes the LibrePhone project;
Table 2, at the end of the section, presents the comparative mapping; Figures 1 and 2
illustrate, respectively, the resulting digital sovereignty stack and the methodological
parallel.
3.1 Two isomorphic trust deficits
 Under the lens of trust theory, the binary blob and the unverified AI agent are the same
object: an artifact whose internal function is not examinable by the user, and about which
the user can only form beliefs through the indirect evidence supplied by the vendor. In the
blob's case, opacity is material — the compiled binary is not, in practice, studyable; the


=== PAGINA 457 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 457
freedom to study guaranteed by the licenses of the upper stack does not reach the lower
layer (LineageOS, 2026; GNU, n.d.). In the agent's case, opacity is statistical and
organizational — even when the model's weights are published, the behavior of the running
system is a function of billions of parameters, of execution data, and of external tools, so
that no exhaustive static examination is feasible (Oliveira, 2026a). In both cases the
consequence is identical: the only available path to trust is the vendor's promise — exactly
what both projects set out to eliminate. Figure 2, further ahead, synthesizes the
methodological parallel between the two cycles.
Schematic figure described in the original artifact: Figure 2 — Methodological parallel: the conversion
of trust into evidence operates by substitution (LibrePhone) or by continuous proof (the VTK), with an
identical logical form (the author's own elaboration).
 The symmetry extends to the typology of harm. The XZ Utils incident demonstrates
that open-source code, when the review process is captured, can incorporate malicious
behavior invisible to casual inspection (NVD, 2024) — the firmware analogue is the blob
whose content no one but the vendor knows. The Bybit incident demonstrates that approval
interfaces can diverge from the real effect of the approved action (FBI, 2025) — the
AI-agent analogue is the divergence between what the model declares and what it executes.
At both poles, the failure mechanism is the absence of an independent verification path
between declaration and reality. It is this structure — not any superficial technological
resemblance — that justifies treating LibrePhone and the VTK as instances of the same
research program.
3.2 Parallel methods: clean-room reverse engineering and
verification by execution
 LibrePhone's method is institutionalized clean-room reverse engineering: binary
analysis by one team, production of specifications and free implementation by another,
with the project's tools supporting the analytical phase (Savoye, 2026). The legal basis is
the Accolade precedent, which protects interoperability-oriented disassembly as legitimate
use (Justia, 1992). The result is not merely a functional substitute: it is the reconquest, for
the user, of the four freedoms over a component that previously denied them — the
replaced blob becomes studyable, modifiable, and redistributable (FSF, 2025a).
 The VTK attacks the same problem by a different and complementary route: instead of
replacing the opaque artifact, it surrounds it with verifiable proofs. The documentation
describes the cycle invariants → falsifiers → verification by execution: properties the agent
must satisfy are declared; computational adversaries (falsifiers) attempt to produce
counterexamples; actual execution is recorded in immutable structures (the WormGraph)
that allow any third party to re-verify the evidence chain (Oliveira, 2026a). The difference
of route — substitution in LibrePhone, continuous proof in the VTK — does not conceal


=== PAGINA 458 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 458
the identity of logical form: both convert the user-system relationship from trust in
promises to trust in evidence. Indeed, the two methods can compose: firmware replaced by
a free implementation still needs integrity verification in execution; an attested model still
benefits from examinable source code. Figure 2 schematizes this parallel.
3.3 Verifiable catalogs: from the blob database to model
attestation
 Perhaps the most directly exploitable convergence lies in catalog infrastructure. Before
any substitution, LibrePhone produces a structured database of the blobs — location in the
image, inferred function, dependencies, versions, exportable to CSV and queryable with
standard tools (LibrePhone, 2026; Savoye, 2026). This inventory fulfills three functions: (i)
epistemic, by transforming diffuse opacity into a finite, addressable list; (ii) organizational,
by allowing reverse engineering targets to be prioritized by criticality; and (iii) auditing, by
making the project's progress measurable (how many blobs cataloged, how many replaced).
 The VTK, in turn, defines the arkhe.attestation.* format for AI models — content
identity, signature, provenance, and declared capabilities — but, as recorded in the project's
documentation, it still lacks a public catalog that aggregates these attestations at scale
(Oliveira, 2026a). The correspondence is evident: LibrePhone's blob database is the
already-operating model of what the VTK's public model catalog intends to be. Both
belong to a family of transparency infrastructures whose precedents include the NVD for
vulnerabilities, transparency logs such as Rekor for signed artifacts (Sigstore, 2026), and
the firmware resiliency guidelines of NIST SP 800-193, which presuppose inventory and
verification of firmware components as a condition for protection, detection, and recovery
(NIST, 2018). The practical implication is the central argument of Section 4: the metadata
schema validated by LibrePhone can be studied as a basis for the model attestation catalog.
3.4 Hardware integration: WPSS, CopyEngine, and the
physical root of trust
 LibrePhone's research documentation on the WPSS and the CopyEngine has relevance
that exceeds the immediate goal of firmware freedom. The WPSS is the processor
subsystem dedicated to wireless functions on Qualcomm platforms, carrying its own
firmware (the wpss.b01–b05 variants) and managed by the Linux kernel's remoteproc
framework (LibrePhone, 2026; Qualcomm, 2025); the CopyEngine performs memory
transfers autonomously with respect to the CPU. Components such as these are exactly the
points of the stack where any hardware attestation mechanism — TPM modules, trusted
execution environments, HSMs — must anchor its chain of trust (NIST, 2018; TCG, n.d.).
Free, documented specifications of these components reduce the area of unverifiable
assumption that any upper attestation layer inherits.


=== PAGINA 459 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 459
 For the VTK, whose architecture provides for artifact verification in contained
execution (including the arkhe-verify-wasm module) and potential hardware anchoring,
LibrePhone's research offers documentary raw material: by cataloging what each
subsystem firmware does — and by proposing inspectable free implementations — the
project converts part of the physical substrate of computing from black box into verifiable
surface (LibrePhone, 2026; Oliveira, 2026a). The resulting stack — specified and
replaceable firmware, a free operating system, an attested agent layer — is illustrated in
Figure 1. It must be acknowledged, however, that full integration between application
attestation and firmware attestation is an open problem, to which Section 5 returns.
3.5 License and governance alignment
 The fifth isomorphism is legal-organizational. The dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 licensing
of the VTK's components places the project, in terms of freedom, within the space of
permissive licenses approved by the Open Source Initiative and compatible, in the case of
Apache-2.0, with GPLv3 in a single direction: Apache-2.0 code can be incorporated into
GPLv3 projects, but not the reverse (Apache Software Foundation, n.d.). This
configuration allows kernel components to be incorporated into GNU ecosystem projects
without license conflict — a necessary, though not sufficient, condition for any integration
with LibrePhone or reuse of its specifications (FSF, 2025a; Oliveira, 2026a).
 The governance dimension is equally relevant. Among the institutions of the free
software ecosystem, the FSF is the one with the strictest criteria regarding software
freedom — its informal certification (endorsement, listing as a high-value project, hosting
of research under its domain) functions as external validation of principled alignment (FSF,
2025b; GNU, n.d.). For the VTK, whose documentation declares compatibility with these
requirements, participation in the LibrePhone ecosystem would constitute a channel of
independent validation at low marginal cost — an argument developed in Section 4.3.
Table 2, below, consolidates the structural mapping of this section; Figure 1 situates the
two projects in the technological stack.

4. Concrete Applications and Strategic
Recommendations
 If the structural convergence of Section 3 holds, it is not merely a descriptive finding: it
generates work items. This section derives from the mapping three concrete applications
for the VTK — corresponding to three capabilities LibrePhone already demonstrates in
operation — and consolidates the resulting recommendations, with priorities and
justifications, in Table 3. The prioritization criterion combines two axes: the application's
technical dependence on artifacts already existing in LibrePhone (the greater, the more
immediate the recommendation) and the estimated integration cost (the lower, the higher
the priority).
4.1 The blob database as a model for the model-attestation
catalog
 The application of highest identified impact is the study of LibrePhone's blob database
as the structural model for the VTK's public model catalog. As described in Section 2.4, the
project's tools import into a database — with bindings for Python and Postgres and CSV
export — metadata on each proprietary component: location in the image, function,
dependencies, and provenance (LibrePhone, 2026; Savoye, 2026). The arkhe.attestation.*
format already defines the verifiable identity of an AI model (hash, signature, provenance,
declared capabilities), but the documentation acknowledges the absence of a public catalog
that aggregates these attestations at scale (Oliveira, 2026a). The parallel suggests a low-risk
engineering exercise with high informational yield: mapping the blob database's metadata
schema — which has already passed the test of real use in an analogous domain — onto the
fields of the attestation format, identifying correspondences, gaps, and necessary
extensions.
 Three extensions seem a priori unavoidable in the mapping. First: while a blob is
essentially static, an AI model has a richer life cycle (fine-tuning, quantization,
derivatives), requiring provenance relations between artifacts — an area in which the
WormGraph's graph structure, with SHA-256 content addressing, offers a native


=== PAGINA 461 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 461
mechanism (Merkle, 1987; Oliveira, 2026a). Second: model attestation requires fields
declaring capabilities and limits that have no direct analogue in firmware. Third: the model
catalog must anchor in a public transparency log — the role Rekor plays in the
WormGraph architecture (Sigstore, 2026) — whereas the blob database is, as far as the
documentation indicates, a research artifact distributed by export. The comparative study of
the two schemas is therefore not copying but informed hybridization — and carrying it out
is the concrete content of Recommendation 1 of Table 3.
4.2 Adapting the analysis tools
 The second application is the assessment of adapting LibrePhone's analysis tools to the
domain of AI artifacts. extractor.py and query_dev.py implement a generic and valuable
work pattern — batch ingestion of binary artifacts, metadata cataloging, and structured
query — which is, in the abstract, exactly what a model inventory requires (LibrePhone,
2026; Savoye, 2026). The adaptation, however, is not trivial: firmware blobs are typically
executable images with known packaging formats, whereas models such as those in GGUF
format are large tensor structures whose relevant metadata (architecture, quantization,
tokenizer, training provenance) reside in headers and external identities. The
recommendation is therefore deliberately prudent: a feasibility study preceding any code
reuse, with the hypothesis that the primary value lies in the work pattern and the database
schema, not in the extraction routines proper.
4.3 Participation in the ecosystem as a channel for external
validation
 The third application is institutional. The VTK documentation declares licensing
compatibility (MIT OR Apache-2.0) with the FSF's freedom criteria (Oliveira, 2026a), and
Apache-2.0 is recognized as compatible with GPLv3 in the sense relevant for incorporation
into the GNU ecosystem (Apache Software Foundation, n.d.). Participation in the
LibrePhone ecosystem — through the project's public channels, such as the IRC channel
indicated in the documentation (Savoye, 2026) — offers the VTK three gains potentially
asymmetric relative to cost: external validation by one of the most rigorous institutions in
verifying software freedom; visibility with the public most technically concerned with
verifiability; and early access to firmware specifications produced by the research (FSF,
2025b; LibrePhone, 2026). As with any institutional alignment, the gain is conditional on
effective consistency between declaration and practice — a condition that, in the VTK's
case, is precisely what the project proposes to demonstrate.
4.4 Consolidated recommendations


=== PAGINA 462 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 462
 Table 3 consolidates the four resulting recommendations, including the formal
documentation of the convergence itself — a governance practice aligned with the VTK's
recording of architecture decisions and with the project's internal strategic analysis
(Oliveira, 2026b). Note that Recommendation 1 is simultaneously the highest-priority and
the lowest-risk: it is a comparative study of schemas, with no commitment to immediate
integration, whose product (a documented mapping between two catalog formats) has value
even if the integration never materializes.

problem — anchoring application chains of trust in verifiable firmware bases — whose
formal treatment would depend on the maturing of both lines (LibrePhone, 2026; NIST,
2018; TCG, n.d.).
5. Counterarguments and Limitations
 The convergence thesis, like any applied research proposal, must be confronted with
serious objections. This section discusses four: the techno-economic viability of reverse
engineering at scale; the conceptual distinction between verifying code and verifying
stochastic behavior; the integrated-security counterargument, propagated by hardened
mobile platforms; and the methodological limitations of the present study. None of the
objections, it is argued, invalidates the thesis — but all of them delimit its scope and
condition the recommendations of Section 4.
5.1 The techno-economic viability of reverse engineering at
scale


=== PAGINA 463 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 463
 The most direct objection is one of cost. A contemporary smartphone carries dozens to
hundreds of blobs; SoCs are renewed annually; and the experience of the precursor
Replicant — whose device support was drastically restricted, precisely because of the cost
of component replacement — indicates that the production of free firmware
implementations does not scale by simply adding volunteers (Replicant, 2026). LibrePhone
is, at the time of writing, essentially a one-veteran-developer project with institutional
hosting by the FSF (FSF, 2025a; Savoye, 2026), and the documentation itself qualifies its
assessments as preliminary and subject to revision (LibrePhone, 2026). The speed of
reverse engineering — artisanal, document by document — competes with the industrial
speed of new platform releases.
 The answer to this objection is twofold and partial. First: LibrePhone's design already
incorporates Replicant's lesson by shifting the goal from replacing everything to cataloging
everything and replacing by priority — the database produces epistemic and organizational
value even without any substitution (Section 3.3). Second: the convergence with projects
such as the VTK broadens, in principle, the base of interest and funding for the cataloging
infrastructure — the blob catalog would cease to be an input exclusive to firmware freedom
research and would come to feed agent attestation as well. This is a hypothesis of project
ecology, not a guarantee: if the cross-demand does not materialize, the objection remains
standing, and LibrePhone's strategy will once again have resulted in restricted coverage.
5.2 Verifying code is not verifying stochastic behavior
 The second objection attacks the VTK side and, by extension, the validity of the
isomorphism. In the firmware domain, verification — by substitution or by inspection —
operates over deterministic artifacts: given the same binary and the same input, the
behavior is the same. In the AI agent domain, identity attestation (hash of weights,
signature) proves that the loaded model is the declared one; it proves nothing about the
correctness of its behavior, which is a function of context, tools, execution data, and the
very stochastic nature of inference. The VTK's cycle of invariants and falsifiers (Section
3.2) mitigates the problem by transforming statements into testable properties and into
recorded execution evidence (Oliveira, 2026a) — but the coverage of a set of invariants is
always partial relative to the space of possible behaviors.
 This objection is conceptually sound and must be incorporated, not refuted. It
establishes that the convergence between LibrePhone and the VTK is one of form — the
conversion of trust into evidence — and not of guarantee: the verifiable evidence of
replaced firmware is stronger than the verifiable evidence of an attested agent. For the
purposes of this part's argument, however, the relevant consequence is preserved: in both
domains, the direction of movement is the same, and the distance between the guarantee
regimes is itself an object of research (which properties of a stochastic agent can, in


=== PAGINA 464 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 464
principle, be the object of verifiable attestation?). The conceptual honesty demanded here
is, incidentally, coherent with the project's motto: prove, don't promise — including about
what can be proven.
5.3 The integrated-security counterargument
 The third objection comes from the mobile security community. Platforms such as
GrapheneOS argue that a device's practical security depends less on the purity of licenses
and more on the quality of the delivery and update chain: vendor-signed blobs, mandatory
verified boot, timely patches — elements that a freedom-oriented project can, in concrete
scenarios, degrade by replacing components for which it assumes no maintenance
responsibility (GrapheneOS, 2026). Under this view, firmware reverse engineering could
reduce users' effective security, exchanging industrially maintained binaries for
community-maintained reimplementations — reproducing, at the firmware level, the
classic debate between freedom and security that runs through the entire free software
movement.
 The objection deserves two answers. The first is empirical: the choice is not binary, and
LibrePhone's design — specifications and cataloging before substitution, dated and
qualified assessments (LibrePhone, 2026) — is precisely the design that allows
distributions to decide, case by case, when substitution improves the security posture (e.g.,
blobs abandoned by the vendor) and when it does not. The second is conceptual and
connects with this part's central thesis: vendors' integrated security is delegated trust — the
user verifies that the device corresponds to what the vendor signed, but cannot verify what
the signed artifact actually is. Mechanisms such as Play Integrity and vendor verified boot
concentrate the root of trust in the vendor; the stack proposed here shifts the root to the
user, by means of public catalogs, free implementations, and independent attestation. The
point is not to deny the value of integrated security — it is to make it complementary, not
alternative, to sovereign verifiability.
5.4 Legal and methodological limitations of this study
 Finally, the limitations of the study itself. First: this is a comparative documentary
analysis — it involved no reverse engineering of its own, no execution of the LibrePhone
tools, and no independent audit of the VTK's statements, whose technical documentation is
internal to the project and is held on record by the author (Oliveira, 2026a; Oliveira,
2026b). The statements about how the two projects work therefore inherit the reliability of
their documentary sources. Second: the object is moving on two scales — LibrePhone is a
recently announced project whose database and technical assessments are still evolving
(Savoye, 2026), and the AI regulatory ecosystem is in transition, with the transparency
obligations of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 applicable from August 2026 (European Union,


=== PAGINA 465 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 465
2024; AI Act Explorer, 2026). Third: the legal framing uses a U.S. precedent (Justia, 1992)
as reference; the legality of reverse engineering varies by jurisdiction, and generalization to
other regimes — including the Brazilian one — would require its own analysis. Fourth: the
author of this part is also the author of the VTK documentation; although the effort at
impartiality is explicit — the objections of Sections 5.2 and 5.3 are intentional and
substantive — the reader should weigh the possible proximity bias. These limitations
delimit the reach of the conclusions and motivate the validation agenda presented next.
6. Conclusion and Implications
 This part proposed and examined the thesis that LibrePhone (FSF) and the VTK
constitute instances of the same structural principle — the conversion of trust into
verifiable evidence — applied to distinct layers of the computing stack. The analysis
identified functional isomorphisms along four dimensions: the trust deficit attacked
(sourceless binaries; opaque stochastic models), the method (clean-room reverse
engineering grounded in the Accolade precedent; verification by execution with invariants
and falsifiers), the production of auditable public catalogs (a blob database; model
attestation), and license and governance alignment (the FSF ecosystem; MIT OR
Apache-2.0). The mapping is not an empty analogy: it generated concrete applications —
with emphasis on the study of the blob database schema as the basis for the public model
attestation catalog — and prioritized recommendations, sustained even in the face of the
objections examined.
 The overall picture is that of an emerging digital sovereignty stack: at the base,
specified and progressively replaceable firmware (LibrePhone); in the middle, free
operating system distributions that can consume those specifications (Replicant,
LineageOS, and successors); at the top, attested and auditable AI agents (the VTK). Each
layer reinforces the others — verifiable firmware anchors the hardware attestation the agent
layer needs; model catalogs extend the transparency the blob catalog inaugurates. The
user's digital sovereignty, in the formulation adopted here (EPRS, 2023), ceases to be a
slogan and becomes an architectural property: the capacity to examine, verify, and — when
necessary — replace each link of the chain on which digital life rests.
 Three implications follow. For research, the immediate agenda includes: (i) the formal
mapping between the blob database schema and the arkhe.attestation.* format, with a
hybrid catalog pilot; (ii) empirical blob coverage metrics (cataloged, specified, replaced) as
a measure of firmware sovereignty progress; and (iii) formal investigation of the open
problem of anchoring application attestation in firmware attestation (WPSS, CopyEngine;
NIST, 2018; TCG, n.d.). For public policy, the convergence suggests that digital
sovereignty initiatives — such as those under way in the European Union, whose AI Act


=== PAGINA 466 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 466
imposes transparency obligations on general-purpose systems and models from August
2026 (European Union, 2024; AI Act Explorer, 2026) — would do well to treat technical
verifiability (catalogs, attestation, transparency logs) as infrastructure complementary to
regulation, rather than as a mere compliance detail. For the free software and AI security
communities, finally, this part's argument is an invitation to collaboration: the conceptual
tools — and, increasingly, the technical tools — of one field are those of the other.
 Forty years after the formulation of the four freedoms, the problem they attacked — the
impossibility of studying what governs our computing — reappears in a new incarnation, in
the form of autonomous agents that act on users' behalf. LibrePhone shows that the
classical answer — specify, implement freely, replace — remains viable at the physical
base of the stack. The VTK shows that it extends, by way of verifiable attestation, to the
stochastic domain at the top. Between the root and the top, the same wager: that trust, to
deserve the name, must be proof.

PART XX — ADJACENT APPLICATIONS
AND GOVERNANCE DOCUMENTS
The verification-first discipline does not live in one field. This part condenses six project
documents, written as independent governance and research papers, into a single account
of how the same epistemic standard — name the number, define the test, record the verdict
— migrates across domains. A proposal to the World Health Organization and BRICS
organizes redox research around a four-layer infrastructure with a US$ 10.05 million
three-phase budget. A lunar-economy monograph separates sovereign from nominal
orchestration under Brazil's emerging AI statute. A smartphone R&D; roadmap treats
product requirements as constitutional invariants with quorums and timelocks. A
documentation audit converts article-level dispositions into telemetry-driven waves. A
topological triage of constitutional amendments computes veto distances and winding
numbers over the text of the 1988 Constitution and its transitional act. And a falsificationist
audit of Ganzfeld meta-analyses shows what VFG-style thresholds would demand of a
controversial literature.
1. A Unified Electron-Transfer Framework for
WHO and BRICS Cooperation
 The first adjacent document is a technical-programmatic dossier prepared for
submission to the World Health Organization and to the health-cooperation mechanisms of
BRICS (internal corpus, on file). Its starting diagnosis is conceptual rather than financial:
cellular redox state is routinely compressed into a single scalar, from which follows the
recurrent clinical counsel to flood the system with generic antioxidants, and hence the
repeated failure of unstratified antioxidant supplementation in clinical trials. Contemporary
redox biology sustains the opposite reading — the state of the system is a vector of
oxidized/reduced ratios (NAD+/NADH, NADP+/NADPH, GSH/GSSG, TrxSS/TrxSH)
resolved by compartment, and both oxidative and reductive excess are genuine pathological
regimes. The dossier generalizes the point institutionally: research itself is fragmented, and
the missing ingredient is not new science but the infrastructure that would make
measurements comparable. The verification-first governance (VFG) framework supplies
the editorial criterion throughout — external claims are anchored to verified sources, and
numbers that exist only in the project's own corpus are flagged as such.
1.1 Four layers and a minimal viable ontology
 The proposed infrastructure is organized in four interdependent layers in a dependency
chain that is explicitly iterative: standardized measurement, interoperable data, multiscale


=== PAGINA 469 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 469
modeling, and design/engineering. Layer 1 attacks reproducibility in three sub-directions
— a reference cell line with isogenic variants expressing genetically encoded biosensors
for the glutathione and NAD+/NADH couples; a reference lot of delaminated Ti3C2Tx with
a mandatory reporting checklist and a round-robin across at least five laboratories; and
expanded substrate scope with pharmacological validation for the redox-neutral synthesis
of aminocyclopropanes. Layer 2 defines a minimal viable ontology of nine core classes
(RedoxCouple, Compartment, Measurement, Calibration, Biosensor, Sample, Condition,
Uncertainty, Metadata), serialized in OWL 2 RL — chosen to maximize interoperability
with production triple stores — and validated by SHACL shapes that make calibration and
co-measured pH mandatory, with modular extensions aligned to SBPAX, EMMO and
BattINFO and FAIR-compliant deposit with DOI on Zenodo. Layer 3 proposes a common
electron-transfer interface — rate as a function of driving force, reorganization energy and
electronic coupling — bridging biological kinetics and materials-scale simulation,
validated against the microperoxidase-11/graphene model system. Layer 4 converts the
stack into design criteria: multiobjective optimization must treat reactive oxygen species
load, redox-pair potentials and cell viability as explicit constraints, because optimizations
that maximize yield while collapsing cellular homeostasis are project failures, not accidents
(internal corpus, on file).
 The dossier is explicit that some load-bearing numbers come from internal or indirectly
cited sources: the MXene performance band — volumetric capacitances from roughly 350
F cm-3 in paper electrodes to about 900 F cm-3 in LiF/HCl clay films, MXene/PANI
composites near 503 F g-1 with 98.3% retention over 10,000 cycles, and HER
overpotentials of 27 mV at 10 mA cm-2 — as well as the RIFD metabolic-engineering
result (L-threonine at 117.65 g/L in Escherichia coli, yield 0.65 g/g, growth restored) are
marked “internal corpus, on file” and scheduled for primary verification before formal
submission. The same honesty applies to the neuroscience numbers below.
1.2 Governance across two institutions and five jurisdictions
 Institutionally the proposal connects three levels. The World Health Organization
provides normative coordination: the 2022 data-sharing policy (WHO, 2022), the CIOMS
ethical guidelines in their fourth edition (CIOMS, 2016), Good Clinical Laboratory Practice
for the consortium's standard operating procedures, and prospective registration of the
clinical pilot on the ICTRP platform. BRICS provides political legitimacy and financing
through the New Development Bank, the STI Framework Programme and the precedent of
thematic networks such as the BRICS Tuberculosis Research Network; that coordination
works at scale is argued from the Solidarity Trial, which randomized 11,330 participants
across 405 hospitals in 30 countries (WHO Solidarity Trial Consortium, 2021). Decision
rules are an operational contract rather than a declaration of intent: ordinary decisions


=== PAGINA 470 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 470
require a quorum of at least three countries and extraordinary decisions four; consensus is
preferred with a two-thirds fallback; disputes rise through WHO mediation to international
arbitration; exit requires twelve months' notice with deposited data remaining in the
repository; and non-compliance escalates to exclusion after three formal warnings (internal
corpus, on file). Because the pilot manipulates health data in five jurisdictions, the dossier
maps them country by country — LGPD with ANPD Resolution CD/ANPD 19/2024 in
Brazil, the DPDP Act 2023 in India, the PIPL-CSL-DSL ecosystem with CAC security
assessment in China, POPIA in South Africa, and 152-FZ localization in Russia —
recommending anonymized data as the international currency, a dedicated legal working
group, and hosting in BRICS-region clouds with at least two replicated regions.
1.3 The three-phase program and its budget
 The implementation program runs sixty months in three phases with an indicative
consolidated budget of US$ 10.05 million, of which personnel is the dominant block at
US$ 5.4 million (54%), followed by infrastructure at US$ 1.2 million, travel and meetings
at US$ 750,000, reference materials at US$ 700,000, translation at US$ 600,000,
publication at US$ 450,000 and a 10% contingency of US$ 950,000 (internal corpus, on
file). Phase 1 (months 0–18) builds the institutional and technical minimum: the founding
charter, committees, at least three data-sharing agreements, at least seven GCLP-aligned
redox SOPs, the ontology minimum in month 6 with the redox and materials extensions in
months 12 and 18, and at least 50 professionals certified in module M0. Phase 2 (months
18–36) executes the multinational clinical pilot; Phase 3 (months 36–60) expands coverage
to at least six redox pairs and five compartments and converts adoption into mandates — at
least three partner journals and funders requiring ontological deposit, on the PDB
precedent. Three transversal indicators span the program: data-deposit compliance of at
least 90%, ontology adoption in at least 50% of consortium articles, and interlaboratory
reproducibility of at least 80% of key findings under independent replication.

1.4 The neuroscience extension and the falsifiable pilot
 The pilot design is where the dossier's verification discipline is most visible. The
consolidated protocol deliberately downgrades ambition to what can be measured
non-invasively in humans: a 3T field — more available in BRICS countries than 7T —
targeting the medial prefrontal cortex and hippocampus, with total glutathione by magnetic
resonance spectroscopy as primary biomarker and lactate as a mitochondrial-bioenergetics
proxy; NAD+ remains exploratory, plasma FRAP is a complementary systemic marker, and
blood glutathione is explicitly not used as a brain proxy, cohort evidence indicating low
correlation between peripheral and central measures (internal corpus, on file). The strongest
counterargument — that genetically encoded biosensors do not cross the blood–brain
barrier — is answered by design rather than rhetoric: MRS of GSH and lactate are the
validated human modalities, with cerebrospinal fluid reserved for clinical indication. The
dossier declares the limits of its primary modality: a voxel of roughly 2 × 2 × 2 cm3 that
does not resolve sub-regions, total rather than oxidized glutathione, pH and temperature
sensitivity, and five to ten minutes per voxel; and it concedes that cerebral mitochondria
remove hydrogen peroxide predominantly through the Trx2/Prx3 system — approximately
60% ± 20% of detoxification, not measurable in vivo — which reserves the thioredoxin
arm for pre-clinical validation and keeps GSH and lactate as proxies. The pilot is falsifiable
in the VFG sense: prospective ICTRP registration precedes recruitment; SHACL shapes
must pass on real clinical data; the ≥ 80% interlaboratory reproducibility threshold is
declared before the round-robin begins; and the Phase 2 dataset with DOI and the
peer-reviewed position paper are politically protected milestones on the critical path.
2. Cognitive Orchestration and the Lunar
Economy
 The second adjacent document is a technical monograph on how Brazil might
coordinate existing but fragmented capabilities for the emerging lunar economy (internal
corpus, on file). Its market frame is deliberately borrowed from verified projections:
consultancy estimates reported in the trade press place annual lunar revenue at up to US$
127.3 billion by 2050 (SatNews, 2026), and the monograph treats that figure not as a
forecast to be defended but as evidence that the Moon is consolidating as an economic and
normative arena in which services — navigation, communication, energy, samples, food,
launch and in-situ resource utilization — are organized by value chains and by rules of


=== PAGINA 472 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 472
conduct. Brazil acceded to the Artemis Accords on June 15, 2021 as the twelfth nation, and
the dossier's question is accordingly not whether the Moon will become an economy but at
which position in the value chain the country will insert itself.
2.1 The national inventory and its asymmetries
 The inventory of national components is more robust than current perception suggests,
though asymmetric in maturity. At the space edge, the SelenITA CubeSat of the
Aeronautics Institute of Technology carries the LINNA payload — a lightweight neural
network identifying surface landmarks from nadir imagery to feed a Visual SLAM
pipeline, providing an independent state estimate in very low lunar orbit, where mascons
make uncorrected low orbits unstable within months to years. At the agronomic edge, the
Space Farming Brazil network, established in 2022 under Embrapa leadership, gathers
roughly 60 researchers working on resilient crops such as sweet potato and chickpea. At the
logistics edge, the Alcântara launch center retains its documented equatorial advantage and
hosted the Innospace HANBIT-Nanor operations (21.8 m, about 20 t), whose first
commercial attempt in December 2025 ended in an accident followed by an agreement for
a new launch in 2026. At the computational and institutional edge, the Brazilian AI Plan
foresees R$ 23 billion between 2024 and 2028, including a supercomputer of 7,200
petaflops in FP16 precision — more than 50,000 cores, acquired for R$ 1 billion for the
Augusto Severo technology park (RN) — and a Brazilian Cloud; and the AEB/Finatec
Aerospace Innovation Hub, announced in June 2026 at PCTec/UnB, includes laboratories,
satellite command and monitoring, supercomputing and regulatory experimentation spaces.
The dossier's verdict is the monograph's thesis: the bottleneck is not the existence of
components but their orchestration and governance (internal corpus, on file).
2.2 Three planes and the regulatory frame
 The proposed architecture distributes cognition across three planes with explicit
interface contracts. The intention plane hosts the central orchestrator — a large language
model with tool augmentation that decomposes mission objectives into validated task
graphs — with human approval points embedded in the graph for high-risk tasks. The
execution plane hosts the domain agents — navigation (LINNA), agriculture (Embrapa),
launch logistics (Alcântara) and in-situ resources — which report state estimates with
confidence values rather than decisions, and execute low-level actions inside pre-approved
envelopes. The infrastructure plane hosts computation (the AI Plan and the Brazilian
Cloud), integration and testing (the Hub as a terrestrial digital twin, where task graphs are
simulated against lunar digital elevation models), and governance. The design is anchored
in peer-reviewed evidence: a three-layer lunar mission architecture in which an LLM with
tool augmentation generates task graphs validated by a ReAct-style framework with


=== PAGINA 473 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 473
decoupled scheduling, and a brain-inspired modular agentic planner whose module
interaction improves planning over competitive baselines (Webb, Mondal and
Momennejad, 2025). On the regulatory side, the monograph maps every component onto
the risk categories of Bill PL 2338/2023 — the Brazilian AI framework approved by the
Senate on December 10, 2024 and sent to the Chamber of Deputies in March 2025 —
classifying the orchestrator, navigation and launch logistics as probable high-risk systems
subject to registration, algorithmic impact assessment, independent auditing and human
supervision, and the agricultural and ISRU agents as ordinary-risk (SENADO FEDERAL,
2024). It further resolves dual compliance with Law 14,946/2024 (BRASIL, 2024), under
which a lunar mission orchestrator would need an AEB license under space law and
registration and assessment under AI law, with audits coordinated between authorities and
the Hub's sandboxes as the compliant development pathway.
2.3 Sovereign versus nominal orchestration
 The monograph's central strategic distinction is between a sovereign orchestrator —
trained in Brazil, on national mission data, over national compute infrastructure, auditable
under Brazilian law — and a nominal orchestrator that merely coordinates foreign
technology even if it physically runs on national soil. The distinction is deliberately
materialist: the AI Plan's supercomputer will be acquired, not developed, so effective
sovereignty resides in the software stack — models, agent tools, interface contracts,
decision records — and in the data, not in the hardware; where the Plan invests its
sovereign-software share therefore decides which orchestrator the country will have
(internal corpus, on file). The monograph is honest that sovereignty is a gradient, not a
binary: control over mission data, adjustment rights, audit records and retraining capacity is
achievable and verifiable even with imported accelerators, and technology transfer is
treated as a contractual condition rather than an expectation.
2.4 Evidence discipline and the four-phase program
 Methodologically the document is notable for its explicit three-level evidence
discipline: claims are marked as documented in primary sources, reported by verified press,
or derived from the internal research corpus, with orchestrator performance metrics — the
elimination of structural violations in generated task graphs and the makespan
improvements from decoupled scheduling — falling in the third class and explicitly
awaiting independent replication (internal corpus, on file). The implementation program
runs in four phases with verifiable success criteria: F0 (2026–2027) establishes governance
— the AEB–ANPD protocol, the sandbox, risk dossiers and the stack decision; F1
(2027–2028) builds the digital twin and requires zero structural violations in a scenario
suite with replicated makespan gains; F2 (2027–2029) flies the edge reference aboard


=== PAGINA 474 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 474
SelenITA/LINNA, requiring state estimation in very low lunar orbit with specified
confidence and documented flight heritage for national embedded AI; F3 (2028–2031)
integrates the complete system under full high-risk audit; and F4 (2030–2035) scales to
services — crop prediction as a continuous service, launch-logistics support, and
contributions to Artemis under the bilateral agreement under negotiation. Transversal
indicators bind the program to its regulatory obligations: 100% of high-risk decisions with
recorded human approval, replanning latency targets by mission class, and
machine-readable evidence coverage for every audit module.

3. A Sovereign Repairable Smartphone: R&D;
Roadmap Under Verification
 The third adjacent document is a critical audit of a 22-month, six-phase research and
development roadmap for a flagship smartphone — audited under the artifact seal
ARKHE-PHONE-RESEARCH-ROADMAP-2026-09-16 (internal corpus, on file). The
roadmap's distinctive move is to treat product documentation as a governed constitution:
eleven document artifacts, each mapped to international engineering standards, are bound
to fifteen ratified constitutional invariants recorded in the ConstitutionStore of the
Verifiable Trust Kernel (VTK) — the append-only, quorum- and timelock-governed
register that gives requirements a status analogous to constitutional amendments.
Amending a performance target costs a simple majority with a short timelock; amending a
security floor costs a reinforced majority and a double window — a direct translation into
product engineering of the principle that reversal costs must be proportional to the risk of
the reversal. The audit's verdict is affirmative with conditions: the method is a replicable


=== PAGINA 475 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 475
contribution to trustworthy device engineering, provided its self-attestation is
complemented by independent validation and its external premises are continuously
reconciled with public metrics.
3.1 The six phases under audit
 The audit reproduces the roadmap faithfully before criticizing it; its synthesis table
appears here as Table 3. The invariants themselves are numerical: INV-FLAG-01 demands
an AnTuTu score of at least 4,500,000 — which the audit situates between 12% and 47%
above public records for the same chipset class, an aggregate reference of 3,057,215 points
against a best individual record of 4,033,382 — ambitious but not implausible for a 2027
product; INV-FLAG-02 a ≥ 200 TOPS (INT8) NPU; INV-FLAG-03 a ≥ 165 Hz, ≥
2,800-nit display; INV-FLAG-04 a ≥ 7,500 mAh silicon-carbon battery rated for ≥ 1,600
cycles; INV-FLAG-05 TPM firmware ≥ 15.25 with dcap-qvl ≥ 0.3.9; and INV-FLAG-06
hybrid post-quantum signatures Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 (NIST, 2024). Governance
parameters are 4/7 or 5/7 quorums among seven guardians with 7- or 14-day timelocks; the
floors ratify security requirements in Phase 0 that Phase 2 will detail — floors before
blueprints, by design.

3.2 Clean-room verification of the external premises
 The audit's method is a clean-room plausibility check: every external premise of the
roadmap is re-derived from public anchors dated 2024–2026, without recourse to any
internal material beyond the roadmap itself. The memory and storage choices survive intact
— LPDDR6 was published by JEDEC in July 2025 (JEDEC, 2025) and UFS 4.1 is
standardized — as do the battery physics, since 7,500 mAh silicon-carbon cells and energy
densities above 900 Wh/L with 32% silicon already exist in 2026 products. Three
divergences are documented with academic honesty rather than smoothed over. First, the


=== PAGINA 476 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 476
market-share premises of the roadmap diverge from the verifiable intervals — public
sources place the leading vendor between 29.4% and 33.7% depending on month and
metric — with reconciliation assigned to the Phase 0 market report and an explicit
definition of metric (shipments versus use) and window. Second, the pilot-fabrication
premise diverges: the roadmap assumes roughly 6 million chips per year for the USP
PocketFab, while the university's own press reported an estimated capacity of 60 million
chips per year for the R$ 89 million facility (Jornal USP, 2026); both series are kept on
record so the correction remains auditable. Third, the roadmap names a future commercial
chipset as launch platform whose specifications were unconfirmed at the access date, and
the audit recommends parameterizing the commercial platform as an interface slot rather
than a named SKU, leaving RISC-V RVA23 — ratified in October 2024 — as the only
named silicon in normative documents.
3.3 The three structural tensions
 Against this generally solid anchor set, the audit identifies three structural tensions.
The schedule tension is the most fundamental: Phase 3 allocates six months to specify and
verify a national RISC-V application SoC, whereas public industrial cycles from
architecture specification to qualified silicon typically exceed two years; the audit's
mitigation is the explicit dual path — the launchable product uses a commercial SoC
architected in Phase 1, while INV-PHONE-03 is reformulated as a strategic-rail invariant
with prototyping milestones at the PocketFab (pre-series in 18–24 months), without
conditioning the Phase 5 gate on tape-out. The benchmark-integrity tension follows from
the same divergence: the audit demands a pre-registered measurement protocol —
benchmark version, thermal curve, number of repetitions, outlier treatment — published
before Phase 4, with raw test logs anchored in the kernel's WormGraph and, ideally,
third-party re-execution; without that pre-registration, compliance with INV-FLAG-01 is
indistinguishable from cherry-picking. The self-attestation tension is epistemic: all fifteen
invariants are ratified and verified by the project's own guardians, and while timelocks,
immutable evidence and public transparency anchors mitigate the risk, a small college can
still by consensus ratify weak evidence; the audit therefore recommends an ISO/IEC
17025-accredited laboratory for the tests sustaining security invariants, publication of test
procedures before Phase 4, and an independent observer seat in the security quorum.
3.4 CVE identifiers as internal codes and the regulatory gate
 Two roadmap identifiers receive a treatment familiar from earlier parts of this book:
the vulnerability identifiers CVE-2026-6726 (TPM 2.0 firmware) and CVE-2026-22696
(the dcap-qvl 0.3.9 quote-verification library) could not be confirmed in public databases at
the audit's access date and are therefore treated as internal premise codes of the program


=== PAGINA 477 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 477
rather than established facts (internal corpus, on file) — the same discipline that keeps
Measured and Unproven statuses distinct. The regulatory gate closes the audit: Phase 5
articulates Anatel homologation of the 5G product, conformity with Act 5,885 of April 29,
2026 on repeaters and anti-interference requirements, the productive-process (PPB) content
score of 662 points for 2025–2027 rising to 689 from 2028, and financing instruments
under Decree 13,065/2026, with the roadmap recording internal financing premises of up to
100% of the project, a 4-year grace period and a 20-year total term pending confirmation in
the actual Brazil Semicon instruments (internal corpus, on file). The audit's closing
observation: this is the only gate whose decision authority is external to the project — the
principal schedule risk, and, if embraced, the program's opportunity, since regulation
already supplies the institutional externality that internal governance cannot. The
consolidated risk register (R1 SoC schedule, R2 unlaunched platform, R3 benchmark
integrity, R4 self-attestation, R5 bill-of-materials and exchange under the US$ 450 ceiling,
R6 mobile regulation) assigns severity and mitigation to each, and the BOM ceiling itself is
flagged for three-scenario sensitivity analysis in Phase 0 — a genuine gap in the
governance catalog, as the audit records.
4. Auditing the Documentation Portfolio: Migrate,
Rewrite, Regenerate, Archive
 The fourth adjacent document answers a management brief with methodological
precision: review an existing documentation set article by article and decide, for each part,
whether to migrate it to a new structure, rewrite it, replace it with output generated from the
code, or archive it; order that work by usage and change frequency with the team manager's
agreement; and design repeatable ways to obtain the knowledge the code simply does not
contain (internal corpus, on file). The paper's thesis is that these three demands are one
problem: an article's disposition and its priority are both functions of the same two
quantities — how much it is used and how fast the world behind it changes — and audits
stall not on the dispositions themselves but on the missing facts that dispositions depend
on.
4.1 Dispositions with triggers
 The disposition taxonomy assigns each article exactly one of four fates, summarized in
Table 4, and three decision rules make it deterministic in practice: type before effort (the
Diátaxis type predicts the feasible set — reference material is a regenerate candidate
wherever a trustworthy machine-readable source exists, explanation almost never); equal
user value, lower maintenance wins (which biases toward regeneration and away from
indefinite rewriting); and never leave stale content live (when evidence is thin, the
conservative default is a labeled snapshot archive, since resurrecting an archived article is


=== PAGINA 478 ===
SHOW THE NUMBER — a verification-first epistemology
Page 478
cheaper than defending inaccurate instructions). Land (2017) supplies the audit tradition
being operationalized: the unit of decision is the article, and audits produce decisions only
when paired with a disposition vocabulary, without which they degenerate into annotated
spreadsheets that age immediately.
